jurisdictions.name: Canada
jurisdictions.office: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
jurisdictions.security_registry: No federal registry: register in the provincial or territorial PPSA registry where the debtor is located (listed below)
jurisdictions.legal_system: Bijural: federal law is read with the common law in the common-law provinces and territories, and with the civil law (the Civil Code of Québec) in Quebec
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a distributing corporation with more than one shareholder); at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians (one, if fewer than four); one or more incorporators; a registered office in the province named in the articles; an annual return each year ($12 online) and a filing of individuals with significant control.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Director assigns a designating number followed by "Canada" and a legal ending, such as 1234567 Canada Inc. (s. 11(2)).
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: federal rates are 15% general and 9% for Canadian-controlled private corporations on the first $500,000 (small business deduction); provincial or territorial tax applies on top where the corporation has a permanent establishment.
jurisdictions.notes: Checked 2026-11-18 by hand. CBCA current to 2026-10-29 (last amended 2026-03-26): s. 102(2) directors, s. 105(3) residency, s. 11(2) designating number, s. 263 annual return. Annual return fee $12 online from Corporations Canada's annual return page. Federal rates from CRA's corporation tax rates page; the $500,000 business limit is the federal standard, not quoted from that page. A federal corporation must also register extra-provincially in each province where it carries on business.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals or bodies corporate may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 7.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall follow the form that the Director fixes and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;
the province in Canada where the registered office is to be situated;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue, and (i) if there will be two or more classes of shares, the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, and (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to, the shares of each series;
if the issue, transfer or ownership of shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement to that effect and a statement as to the nature of such restrictions;
the number of directors or, subject to paragraph 107(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation; and
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: New Brunswick
jurisdictions.security_registry: Service New Brunswick, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (at least three for a reporting issuer), with no residency requirement; one or more incorporators; a registered office in New Brunswick; no minimum capital; an annual return each year.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Director assigns a designating number as the corporation's name (s. 9(2)); the usual form is a number plus a New Brunswick legal ending, but the exact wording was not confirmed officially.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 14%; small business rate 2.5% on the first $500,000 of active business income; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: The laws.gnb.ca consolidation read was marked 'Current to 1 January 2024'. Annual return fee not confirmed from a current official schedule (older SNB forms show $60 online / $80 paper). Numbered-name format (e.g. '123456 N.B. Ltd.') comes only from third-party sources.

who_may_incorporate.text: 3 (1) One or more individuals may incorporate by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 4 if (a) they are not less than 19 years of age, (b) they have not been found incapable of managing their affairs by a court or tribunal in Canada or elsewhere, and (c) they do not have the status of bankrupt. 3 (2) One or more bodies corporate may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 4.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall be in the form provided by the Director and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue and any maximum aggregate amount for which such shares may be issued, and (i) if there will be two or more classes of shares, the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to, the shares of each series, (iii) if the shares will be of one kind only, the par value of each share or a statement that the shares are without par value, and (iv) if the shares are of both kinds, any maximum number of shares of each kind, the par value of each share having par value and a statement that the other kind of shares are without par value;
if the issue, transfer or ownership of the shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement to that effect and a statement as to the nature of the restrictions;
the number of directors or any minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation; and
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
jurisdictions.security_registry: Government Services, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a distributing corporation); no director residency rule since 2021; one or more incorporators; a registered office in the province; no minimum capital; an annual return each year ($100).
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the registrar assigns a designating number as the corporation's name (s. 20); the exact form of the numbered name was not confirmed from an official source.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 15%; small business rate 2% (cut from 2.5% on January 1, 2026) on the first $500,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: The resident-Canadian director rule (old s. 174) was repealed by SNL 2021 c26 s4. Annual return fee of $100 (local corporation with share capital, since 2017) is from https://www.gov.nl.ca/gs/registries/companies/annual-returns/.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals or 1 or more bodies corporate may incorporate a corporation by signing and sending articles of incorporation to the registrar.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall follow the prescribed form and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;
the place in the province and the address including street name and number where the registered office is to be situated;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue and (i) where there will be 2 or more classes of shares, the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, and (ii) where any class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to, the shares of each series;
where the right to transfer shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement that the right to transfer shares is restricted and the nature of the restrictions;
the number of directors or, where required by paragraph 176(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation; and
a restriction on the business that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: Nova Scotia
jurisdictions.security_registry: Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: Companies Act limited company or unlimited company (ULC): at least one director, no residency rule; one or more subscribers; a Nova Scotia registered office and recognized agent; yearly renewal ($118.35, limited company).
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: the Registry of Joint Stock Companies gives the next available number, in the form '1234567 Nova Scotia Limited'.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 14%; small business rate 1.5% on the first $700,000 (above the $500,000 federal limit); federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: Nova Scotia has no Business Corporations Act; companies (limited by shares, by guarantee, or unlimited/ULC) are formed under the Companies Act (consolidation dated January 20, 2026). The $200 incorporation and $118.35 renewal fees and the recognized-agent requirement are from https://www.novascotia.ca/incorporate-limited-company; the ULC renewal fee was not checked. The 1.5% rate and $700,000 limit took effect April 1, 2025.

articles.document: Memorandum of association and articles of association

who_may_incorporate.text: Any one or more persons associated for any lawful purpose other than a banking, loan, trust or insurance company, may, by subscribing their names to a memorandum of association and otherwise complying with the requirements of this Act in respect of registration, form an incorporated company, with or without liability, …

items.text: the memorandum must state
the name in all its language forms of the company, with “Incorporated”, “Incorporée”, “Limited”, “Limitée”, “Inc.”, “Ltd.” or “Ltée” as the last word in each form of its name,
the restrictions, if any, on the objects and powers of the company,
that the liability of the members is limited,

in the case of a company having par value shares, the amount of share capital of each class of such shares with which the company proposes to be registered and the division thereof into shares of a fixed amount,

in the case of a company having shares without nominal or par value, the maximum number of shares of each class of such shares that the company is authorized to issue or, where there is no limit on the number of shares of any such class, a statement to that effect, and
in the case of a company having both par value shares and shares without nominal or par value, the particulars thereof in accordance with subclauses (iv) and (v);
no subscriber of the memorandum may take less than one share; and
each subscriber must indicate opposite to his name the number of shares he takes, together with his address.
the memorandum must state (i) the name in all its language forms of the company, and (ii) the restrictions, if any, on the objects and powers of the company; and

In the case of an unlimited company, the articles must state (a) in the case of a company having par value shares, the amount of share capital of each class of such shares with which the company proposes to be registered and the division thereof into shares of a fixed amount; (b) in the case of a company having shares without nominal or par value, the maximum number of shares of each class of such shares that the company is authorized to issue or, where there is no limit on the number of shares of any such class, a statement to that effect; and (c) in the case of a company having both par value shares and shares without nominal or par value, the particulars thereof in accordance with clauses (a) and (b).

jurisdictions.name: Prince Edward Island
jurisdictions.security_registry: Atlantic Canada On-Line, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a distributing corporation), no residency rule, but a PEI lawyer's certificate is needed if no director lives in PEI; one or more incorporators; a registered office in PEI; annual return.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Director assigns a designating number as the corporation's name (s. 9(2)); the exact form of the numbered name was not confirmed from an official source.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 15% (cut from 16% on July 1, 2025); small business rate 1% on the first $600,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: Statute read is the Business Corporations Act (RSPEI c. B-6.01), current to June 30, 2026. The PDF does not print subsection numbers, so subsection labels such as s. 4(1) are inferred from cross-references. The $30 annual return fee appears only on an older-looking government page and third-party sites, so it is not stated. The PEI business limit rose from $500,000 to $600,000 on July 1, 2025.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals or bodies corporate or any combination of them may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 5.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall follow the form approved by the Director and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue and any maximum aggregate amount for which the shares may be issued, and (i) if there will be two or more classes of shares, the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class, except in the case of preferred shares authorized by the articles where the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions are to be determined by bylaw at the time of issuance under subsection 31(4), (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in each series, and to determine the designation of, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to, the shares of each series, (iii) if the shares will be of one kind only, the par value of each share or a statement that the shares are without par value, and (iv) if the shares are of more than one kind, any maximum number of shares of each kind, the par value of each share that has a par value and a statement that the other kind or kinds of shares are without par value;
if the issue, transfer or ownership of shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement to that effect and a statement as to the nature of the restrictions;
the number of directors or, subject to clause 82(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation; and
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: Ontario
jurisdictions.security_registry: ServiceOntario, Personal Property Security Registration (Access Now)
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for an offering corporation), with no residency requirement since July 2021; one or more incorporators; a registered office in Ontario; an annual return each year (no fee).
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: a number name is the corporation number followed by 'Ontario' and a legal ending, such as 1234567 Ontario Inc.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general 11.5%; small business rate on the first $500,000 cut from 3.2% to 2.2% on July 1, 2026 (prorated); federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: OBCA read on e-Laws (consolidation period from October 1, 2025; e-Laws currency date November 13, 2026). The residency rule in s. 118(3) was repealed by 2020, c. 34, Sched. 1. The $0 annual return fee is from ontario.ca's 'Cost and time required to register' page (seen via search, not opened). Since 2017 c. 20 s. 5(1) no longer lists the articles' contents; they are set by the Act, the regulations and the Director's approved form.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals or bodies corporate or any combination thereof may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 6.

items.text: Articles of incorporation must be in the form approved by the Director and must set out the information required by this Act, the regulations or the Director.

jurisdictions.name: Quebec
jurisdictions.security_registry: Register of Personal and Movable Real Rights (RDPRM)
jurisdictions.legal_system: Civil law (the Civil Code of Québec) for private law; federal and public law are common law
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a reporting issuer), no residency requirement; one or more founders; head office in Québec; no minimum capital; annual updating declaration (free on time) and registration fee ($106, 2026).
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the enterprise registrar assigns a designating number in lieu of a name, in the form 9XXX-XXXX Québec inc.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general 11.5%; small business 3.2% (2.2% for years starting after April 29, 2026) on the first $500,000, if 5,500 paid hours or primary/manufacturing activity; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: QBCA read on LegisQuébec (updated to October 15, 2026). The 2.2% rate is from Information Bulletin 2026-3 (April 29, 2026) and was announced, not confirmed as enacted. The SBD phases out between 5,500 and 5,000 paid hours. Quebec administers its own corporate tax. The $106 annual registration fee (for-profit legal person, 2026) is from the Registraire's RE-101 schedule. The QBCA allows a designating number (s. 5(1)); the '9XXX-XXXX Québec inc.' form is confirmed only from register examples (e.g. 9426-6111 Québec inc.), not an official page.

who_may_incorporate.text: A corporation may be constituted by one or more founders.

items.text: The articles of constitution must set out
the name of the corporation, unless a designating number in lieu of a name has been requested from the enterprise registrar;
the name and address of each founder, or the name of the founding legal person, the address of its head office and an exact reference to the Act under which it is constituted;
the amount to which its share capital is limited, if applicable;
the par value of its shares, if any;
if there will be two or more classes of shares, the rights and restrictions attaching to the shares of each class;

if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the board of directors to determine, before issue, the number of shares in, the designation of the shares of, and the rights and restrictions attaching to the shares of, each series;
any restrictions on the transfer of its instruments or shares;
the fixed number or the minimum and maximum number of directors; and
any restrictions on its business activity.

jurisdictions.note: A federal corporation may be more powerful than one made in Quebec's civil-law jurisdiction. The Canada Business Corporations Act gives it “the capacity and, subject to this Act, the rights, powers and privileges of a natural person” and says it “may carry on business throughout Canada” (s. 15(1)–(2)), under one name protected across the country. A Quebec corporation is a legal person under the Civil Code of Québec, and outside Quebec it carries on business only as each other province's law allows.

jurisdictions.name: Alberta
jurisdictions.security_registry: Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a widely held reporting issuer), no residency rule since 2021; one or more incorporators; an Alberta registered office and a resident-Albertan agent for service; annual return.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Registrar assigns a designated number as the corporation's name (s. 11), usually in the form 1234567 Alberta Ltd.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 8%, the lowest provincial general rate; small business rate 2% on the first $500,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: ABCA read is current as of September 2, 2026. The 25% resident-Canadian rule was removed effective March 29, 2021, and the agent-for-service rule (s. 20.1) was added. Annual returns are filed through registry agents, who add their own service fee; the government fee was not confirmed. The '1234567 Alberta Ltd.' form was not confirmed from an official source. Alberta's 2026 budget made no corporate rate changes. Alberta, like Quebec, administers its own corporate income tax.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 7.

items.text: Subject to section 15.3, articles of incorporation shall be in the form required by the Registrar and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation,

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue, and (i) if there are 2 or more classes of shares, the special rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, and (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of each series, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to the shares of each series,

if the right to transfer shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement that the right to transfer shares is restricted and either (i) a statement of the nature of the restrictions, or (ii) a statement that the nature of the restrictions appears in a unanimous shareholder agreement,
the number of directors or, subject to section 107(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation, and
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: British Columbia
jurisdictions.office: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry
jurisdictions.security_registry: BC Registries, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a public company), with no residency requirement; one or more incorporators; a registered office and records office in B.C.; no minimum capital; an annual report each year ($43.39).
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: if no name is reserved, the name is the incorporation number followed by 'B.C. Ltd.' (or 'B.C. Unlimited Liability Company'), such as 1234567 B.C. Ltd.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 12%; small business rate 2% on the first $500,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: BCA read on BC Laws (current to November 10, 2026); s. 120 (directors) is in Part 5, s. 34 (offices) and s. 51 (annual report) in Part 2. The $43.39 annual report fee (plus a $1.50 BC OnLine fee) is from a BC government guide, https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/employment-business-and-economic-development/business-management/permits-licences-and-registration/registries-other-assets/how_to_file_an_annual_report.pdf; one older gov.bc.ca page still shows $30. B.C. also allows unlimited liability companies.

articles.document: Incorporation agreement, incorporation application and notice of articles (plus articles)

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may form a company by (a) entering into an incorporation agreement, (b) filing with the registrar an incorporation application, and (c) complying with this Part.

items.text: An incorporation application referred to in subsection (1) (b) must
be in the form established by the registrar,
contain a completing party statement referred to in section 15,
set out the full names and mailing addresses of the incorporators,

set out (i) the name reserved for the company under section 22, and the reservation number given for it, or (ii) if a name is not reserved, a statement that the name by which the company is to be incorporated is the name created, …
contain a notice of articles that reflects the information that will apply to the company on its incorporation.
Unless this Act provides otherwise, the notice of articles of a company must
be in the form established by the registrar,
set out the name of the company,
set out the full name of, and prescribed address for, each of the directors,
identify the registered office of the company by its mailing address and its delivery address,
identify the records office of the company by its mailing address and its delivery address,
set out, in the prescribed manner, any translation of the company's name that the company intends to use outside Canada,
describe the authorized share structure of the company in accordance with section 53, and

set out, in respect of each class and series of shares, whether there are special rights or restrictions attached to the shares of that class or series of shares and, if there are or were special rights or restrictions, set out the date of each resolution altering those special rights or restrictions …

jurisdictions.name: Manitoba
jurisdictions.security_registry: Teranet Manitoba, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a distributing corporation); at least 25% of directors must be Canadian residents (one, if three or fewer); one or more incorporators; a registered office in Manitoba; an annual return each year.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Director assigns a designating number as the corporation's name (s. 11(2)); a legal ending is added, as in 1234567 Manitoba Ltd.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 12%; small business rate 0% on the first $500,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: Manitoba still has the residency rule: s. 100(3) and (3.1) of The Corporations Act (C.C.S.M. c. C225, version current as of November 16, 2026). The annual return fee was not confirmed from a current official schedule (an archived 2008 form showed $40). The '1234567 Manitoba Ltd.' form was not confirmed from an official source; third-party sources say the province assigns the number and the incorporator picks the legal ending.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons, being a body corporate or a natural person, may incorporate a corporation by signing and delivering to the Director articles of incorporation.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall be in the form the Director requires and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;
the place in Manitoba where the registered office is to be situated, and the address, giving the street and number, if any;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue, and (i) if there will be two or more classes of shares, the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, and (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to, the shares of each series;
if the issue transfer or ownership of shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement to that effect, and a statement as to the nature of such restrictions;

the number of directors or, subject to clause 102(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation, and in every case the names in full of each first director and his residence address giving the street and number, if any; and
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: Saskatchewan
jurisdictions.office: Saskatchewan Registries (Information Services Corporation), Corporate Registry
jurisdictions.security_registry: Saskatchewan Registries, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a distributing corporation); no Canadian residency rule since 2023, but an attorney is needed if no director or officer lives in Saskatchewan; one or more incorporators; a Saskatchewan registered office; annual return.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Registrar assigns a designating number followed by 'Saskatchewan' and a legal ending (s. 2-9), such as 101234567 Saskatchewan Ltd.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 12%; small business rate 1% on the first $600,000 (above the $500,000 federal limit); federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: The Business Corporations Act, 2021 (SS 2021, c 6, in force March 12, 2023; unofficial consolidation as amended to 2024 c 4 and c 10) dropped the 25% resident-Canadian rule; s. 9-6(3) requires an attorney if no director or officer lives in Saskatchewan. ISC's 2024 fee schedule lists a $60 for-profit annual return fee, but 2025-26 changes were not checked. ISC says the number is nine digits. The publications.saskatchewan.ca server sends an incomplete TLS chain; the file was fetched after adding DigiCert's public intermediate certificate.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals or bodies corporate may incorporate a corporation by signing and delivering to the Registrar articles of incorporation.

items.text: Articles of incorporation must set out, with respect to the proposed corporation:
the name of the corporation;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue, and: (i) if there will be 2 or more classes of shares, the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares; and (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to, the shares of each series;
if the issue, transfer or ownership of shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement to that effect and a statement as to the nature of those restrictions;
the number of directors or, subject to clause 9-8(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation;
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on or on the powers that the corporation may exercise;
the registered office in accordance with section 4-1;
the initial directors and officers of the corporation, in accordance with section 9-7; and
any other prescribed information.

jurisdictions.name: Northwest Territories
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of Justice, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a distributing corporation), with no residency requirement; one or more incorporators; a registered office in the Northwest Territories; no minimum capital; an annual return each year.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Registrar assigns a designated number with any words it requires as the corporation's name (s. 11(1)), e.g. a number followed by 'N.W.T. Ltd.'
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 11.5%; small business rate 2% on the first $500,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: justice.gov.nt.ca refused connections, so the Act (SNWT 1996, c.19, office consolidation as amended to SNWT 2025, c.2) was read from the Internet Archive copy of the official PDF captured April 6, 2026: https://web.archive.org/web/20260406062310/https://www.justice.gov.nt.ca/en/files/legislation/business-corporations/business-corporations.a.pdf. The 'N.W.T.' form comes from archived 2006 registry guidance. Annual return fee not confirmed.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 7.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall be in the prescribed form and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;
the place within the Northwest Territories where the registered office is to be situated;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue, and (i) if there are two or more classes of shares, the special rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, and (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of each series, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to the shares of each series;

if the issue, transfer or ownership of the shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement to that effect and (i) a statement of the nature of the restrictions, or (ii) a statement that the nature of the restrictions appears in a unanimous shareholder agreement;
