any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: Nunavut
jurisdictions.office: Department of Justice, Legal Registries Division
jurisdictions.security_registry: Legal Registries Division, Personal Property Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a distributing corporation), with no residency requirement; one or more incorporators; a registered office in Nunavut; no minimum capital; an annual return each year.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: on request the Registrar assigns a designated number with any words it requires as the corporation's name (s. 11(1)); the exact form was not confirmed.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 12%; small business rate 3% on the first $500,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: Nunavut's Business Corporations Act (inherited S.N.W.T. 1996, c.19) was read from the Internet Archive copy (April 18, 2025) of the official consolidation, which is current only to February 1, 2015: https://web.archive.org/web/20250418031203/https://www.nunavutlegislation.ca/en/file-download/download/public/617. nunavutlegislation.ca says it is not up to date and lists later amendments (S.Nu. 2017,c.22; 2021,c.19; 2023,c.17; 2025,c.14; 2025,c.15), which were not checked. Annual return fee not confirmed.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 7.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall be in the prescribed form and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;
the place within Nunavut where the registered office is to be situated;

the classes and any maximum number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue, and (i) if there are two or more classes of shares, the special rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, and (ii) if a class of shares may be issued in series, the authority given to the directors to fix the number of shares in, and to determine the designation of each series, and the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to the shares of each series;

if the issue, transfer or ownership of the shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement to that effect and (i) a statement of the nature of the restrictions, or (ii) a statement that the nature of the restrictions appears in a unanimous shareholder agreement;
the number of directors or, subject to paragraph 108(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation; and
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on.

jurisdictions.name: Yukon
jurisdictions.security_registry: Register a personal property lien
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three for a public corporation with more than one shareholder), with no residency requirement; one or more incorporators; a registered office in Yukon; no minimum capital; an annual return each year.
jurisdictions.number_names: Yes: leave the name blank on the articles and the registry assigns a numbered name, such as 45325 Yukon Inc.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 tax year: general rate 12%; small business rate 0% on the first $500,000; federal rates (15% general, 9% small business) apply on top.
jurisdictions.notes: laws.yukon.ca is behind a bot challenge, so the Act (RSY 2002, c. 20, amended to SY 2024, c. 13; unofficial consolidation) was read from the Internet Archive copy of the official PDF captured July 24, 2026: https://web.archive.org/web/20260724211120/https://laws.yukon.ca/cms/images/LEGISLATION/PRINCIPAL/2002/2002-0020/2002-0020.pdf. Its section numbers (s. 7 incorporation, s. 8 articles, s. 22 registered office, s. 102 directors) differ from older versions (s. 5/s. 6). No director residency provision was found. The '45325 Yukon Inc.' example is from a YCOR entity profile. Annual return fee not confirmed.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may incorporate a corporation by signing articles of incorporation and complying with section 9.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall be in the prescribed form and shall set out, in respect of the proposed corporation,
the name of the corporation;

the classes of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue including (i) the maximum number of shares of each class that the corporation is authorized to issue or a statement that the number of shares of that class is unlimited, (ii) the par value of shares of a class with par value or a statement that the shares of that class are without par value, (iii) if there are two or more classes of shares, the special rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to each class of shares, and (iv) if a class of shares may be issued in one or more series, for each series (A) the number of shares in the series, which may be unlimited, and the designation, rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to the shares of the series, or (B) the authority given to the directors to establish the number of shares in the series, and to determine the designation, rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions attaching to the shares in the series;

if the right to transfer shares of the corporation is to be restricted, a statement that the right to transfer shares is restricted and either (i) a statement of the nature of the restrictions, or (ii) a statement that the nature of the restrictions appears in a unanimous shareholder agreement;
the number of directors or, subject to paragraph 108(a), the minimum and maximum number of directors of the corporation; and
any restrictions on the businesses that the corporation may carry on including the restrictions set out in paragraph 18(1)(h) of the Yukon Act (Canada).

jurisdictions.name: Connecticut
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of the State, Business Services
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of the State, UCC filings (Business.CT.gov)
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; officers as the bylaws provide; a registered agent in the state; an annual report each year ($150).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "corporation", "incorporated", "company", "limited" or an abbreviation; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporation business tax 7.5% flat (2026), $250 minimum; 10% surtax for companies with $100M+ gross income or combined groups, extended through income year 2028; capital-base alternative tax being phased out.
jurisdictions.notes: Director minimum (CGS 33-737) and officer rule confirmed via secondary copies of the statute; cga.ct.gov could not be read directly. Capital base tax: DRS shows 2.1 mills for 2025; 2026 rate (reportedly 1.6 mills) or earlier repeal not confirmed. Articles: Read from the official CGA chapter 601 page (statutes revised to January 1, 2026). Items (a)(5) email and (a)(6) NAICS code were added by P.A. 24-111. The site's TLS chain is incomplete; it was read by supplying GoDaddy's published intermediate certificate, with verification left on.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering a certificate of incorporation to the Secretary of the State for filing.

items.text: The certificate of incorporation shall set forth:
A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 33-655;
the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
the street and mailing address of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office;
the name and address of each incorporator;
the valid electronic mail address of the corporation; and
the corporation's North American Industry Classification System Code.

jurisdictions.name: Maine
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of State, Bureau of Corporations, Elections and Commissions
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; no required officer titles (one officer keeps minutes); a registered agent in the state; an annual report each year ($85, due June 1).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which need only be distinguishable on the Secretary of State's records (no corporate suffix is required); numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax in brackets (2026): 3.5% up to $350,000, 7.93%, 8.33%, and 8.93% on income over $3.5 million; no separate franchise tax for general business corporations.
jurisdictions.notes: Officers per 13-C §841; annual report fee $85 per 13-C §123 and the Secretary of State fee table. The 2026 Form 1120W (which would confirm the full bracket table) could not be opened; the revenue FAQ shows the brackets unchanged since 2018, and the Maine Revenue Services 1120W says the same 3.5% first bracket applies to 2026. Articles: Read from the official Maine Revisor's pages (§ 201 at title13-Csec201.html). Item C incorporates 5 M.R.S. § 105(1) (registered agent), quoted from https://legislature.maine.gov/statutes/5/title5sec105.html; the elided part is a bracketed session-law history note. Former paragraph E is repealed.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may serve as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: The articles of incorporation of a corporation must set forth:
A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 401;

The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue and, if there are 2 or more classes of shares, the number of shares and a description of the rights in each class, as provided in section 601, subsection 1;
The information required by Title 5, section 105, subsection 1; and
The name and address of each incorporator.

A clerk or registered agent filing must state: A. The name of the represented entity's commercial clerk or commercial registered agent; or … B. If the entity does not have a commercial clerk or commercial registered agent: (1) The name and address of the entity's noncommercial clerk or noncommercial registered agent; or (2) The title of an office or other position with the entity if service of process is to be sent to the person holding that office or position, and the address of the business office of that person.

jurisdictions.name: Massachusetts
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of the Commonwealth, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One director if one shareholder, two if two, otherwise three (unless articles say otherwise); one or more incorporators; a president, treasurer and secretary (one person may hold all); registered agent; annual report ($125).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "corporation", "incorporated", "company", "limited" or an abbreviation; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate excise (2026): 8% of net income plus $2.60 per $1,000 of taxable tangible property or net worth, with a $456 minimum.
jurisdictions.notes: Officers per 156D §8.40. Annual report $125 is from the Corporations Division fee schedule (updated 2022); some third-party sites list $109 for online filing, which could not be confirmed. No residency or capital requirement found. The 8% rate and $456 minimum come from the state's FY27 tax expenditure budget, not a DOR rate page. Articles: Read from the official malegislature.gov pages (§ 2.01 at .../Section2.01). Massachusetts calls the filing "articles of organization". Under § 2.02(d) the filing form must also give, as supplemental information not part of the articles, the street address of the initial registered office, the initial registered agent, the initial directors, president, treasurer and secretary, the fiscal year, and other information the Secretary requires.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by signing articles of organization and delivering them to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: The articles of organization shall set forth:
a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 4.01;
the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue, and any required description of additional classes or series of shares, in conformity with section 6.01; and
the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: New Hampshire
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC and Statutory Liens
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; officers as the bylaws provide; a registered agent in the state; an annual report each year ($100).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "corporation", "incorporated", "limited" or an abbreviation; numbers may be part of a chosen name, but adding a number alone does not make a name distinguishable.
jurisdictions.tax: Business profits tax 7.5% flat (2026) plus business enterprise tax 0.55% on wages, interest and dividends paid; BPT payable is credited against BET; no sales or general personal income tax.
jurisdictions.notes: Directors per RSA 293-A:8.03, officers per 8.40. BPT 7.5% applies to periods ending on or after Dec 31, 2023. Filing thresholds: BPT reportedly $109,000 gross business income for 2025+ (not confirmed on the DRA site); HB 155 (2026) raises the BET threshold to $400,000 from Jan 1, 2027, per secondary sources. HB 1546 (2026) proposed repealing the BPT; status not confirmed. revenue.nh.gov pages blocked direct reading. Articles: Read from the official General Court RSA pages (§ 2.01 at 293-A-201.htm).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: The articles of incorporation must set forth:
a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of RSA 293-A:4.01;
the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
the street address of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office; and
the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: New Jersey
jurisdictions.office: Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services
jurisdictions.security_registry: Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services, UCC filings
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a president, secretary and treasurer (one person may hold several); a registered agent and office in the state; an annual report each year ($75).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must carry a corporate designator such as "Corporation", "Incorporated", "Company" or an abbreviation; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporation business tax (2026): 9% if entire net income exceeds $100,000 (7.5% if $50,001-$100,000; 6.5% if $50,000 or less); 2.5% corporate transit fee on income over $10 million through 2028; $500-$2,000 minimum.
jurisdictions.notes: Officers confirmed under N.J.S.A. 14A:6-15. Director minimum (14A:6-2) and the exact name-designator list (14A:2-2) could not be read from the statute text (site blocked); stated from standard NJ law. Annual report $75 confirmed only by third-party sources, not the nj.gov fee page; a July 2026 change cut the formation fee ($125 to $100) but reportedly not the annual report fee. Lower 7.5%/6.5% rates confirmed via Treasury pages and a secondary source. Articles: NOT read from the official site: the NJ Legislature's statutes site (lis.njleg.state.nj.us) refused or timed out, and Justia, FindLaw and CounselStack blocked automated reading. Excerpts were read and script-checked against a third-party copy of Title 14A (https://www.hopb.co/new-jersey-business-corporation-act-title-14a), which says it is current through P.L.2025, c.346. The url field gives the Justia page for reference only; it was not read. Also required when they apply: classes and series and board authority over them (1)(d)-(e), duration if not perpetual (1)(j), and a delayed effective date (1)(k). Paragraph (1)(f), optional provisions, is listed in (1) but is elective.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals or domestic or foreign corporations may act as incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by signing and filing in the office of the Secretary of State a certificate of incorporation for such corporation. Individuals acting as incorporators shall be at least 18 years of age. Incorporators need not be United States citizens or residents of this State or subscribers to shares in the corporation.

items.text: The certificate of incorporation shall set forth:
The name of the corporation;

The purpose or purposes for which the corporation is organized. It shall be a sufficient compliance with this paragraph to state, alone or with specifically enumerated purposes, that the corporation may engage in any activity within the purposes for which corporations may be organized under this act, …
The aggregate number of shares which the corporation shall have authority to issue;

The address of the corporation's initial registered office, and the name of the corporation's initial registered agent at such address. … the address of the registered office as shown on the certificate of incorporation shall be a complete address, including the number and street location of the registered office and, if applicable, the post office box number;
The number of directors constituting the first board and the names and addresses of the persons who are to serve as such directors;
The names and addresses of the incorporators;

jurisdictions.name: New York
jurisdictions.office: Department of State, Division of Corporations
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators (natural persons 18 or older); no residency or capital requirement; no required officers; Secretary of State serves as process agent (registered agent optional); biennial statement ($9).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "corporation", "incorporated", "limited" or an abbreviation; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporation franchise tax (2026): 6.5% of business income, 7.25% for business income over $5 million (extended through 2029), or a small capital-base tax or fixed-dollar minimum if higher; New York City taxes separately.
jurisdictions.notes: Directors per BCL §702 (defaults to one). The FY2027 budget (enacted 2026) extended the 7.25% rate and 0.1875% capital-base rate to tax years beginning before 2030; confirmed via law-firm and EY summaries, not a tax.ny.gov page. Officer rule (BCL §715, permissive) and incorporator rule (§401) stated from standard law, not re-read. Articles: NOT read from the official site by script: nysenate.gov (the official source) returned a bot challenge to direct download and would only summarize, and the LBDC public site timed out. Excerpts were read and script-checked against the New York public.law copy (https://newyork.public.law/laws/n.y._business_corporation_law_section_402; § 401 at ..._section_401), which cites nysenate.gov as its source (§ 402 updated Jan. 6, 2023; § 401 updated Sep. 22, 2014). The (a) opening is trimmed because that copy's rendering of the quoted certificate title is garbled by an inserted link. Also required when they apply: classes and their rights (a)(5), preferred series (a)(6), a registered agent if the corporation has one (a)(8), and duration if not perpetual (a)(9). New York does not require a registered agent; the Secretary of State is designated to receive process.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more natural persons of the age of eighteen years or over may act as incorporators of a corporation to be formed under this chapter.

items.text: … shall be signed by each incorporator, with his name and address included in such certificate and delivered to the department of state. It shall set forth:
The name of the corporation.

The purpose or purposes for which it is formed, it being sufficient to state, either alone or with other purposes, that the purpose of the corporation is to engage in any lawful act or activity for which corporations may be organized under this chapter, provided that it also state that it is not formed to engage in any act or activity requiring the consent or approval of any state official, department, board, agency or other body without such consent or approval first being obtained.
The county within this state in which the office of the corporation is to be located.

The aggregate number of shares which the corporation shall have the authority to issue; if such shares are to consist of one class only, the par value of the shares or a statement that the shares are without par value; …

A designation of the secretary of state as agent of the corporation upon whom process against it may be served and the post office address within or without this state to which the secretary of state shall mail a copy of any process against it served upon him or her.

jurisdictions.name: Pennsylvania
jurisdictions.office: Department of State, Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors, who must be adults, and one or more incorporators. No residency or capital requirement. Needs a president, secretary and treasurer, a Pennsylvania registered office or commercial registered office provider, and an annual report ($7).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must be distinguishable on Department of State records; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate net income tax 7.49% flat for tax year 2026, falling 0.5 points a year to 4.99% in 2031; capital stock/franchise tax already repealed.
jurisdictions.notes: The annual report ($7, due by June 30) started in 2025. Third-party sources say no dissolution penalty applies to the 2025-2026 reports, with enforcement from 2027; not confirmed on pa.gov. The officer requirement (15 Pa.C.S. 1732) and director qualifications (15 Pa.C.S. 1722-1723) came from secondary statute copies, not the official text. Articles: Read from the General Assembly's official PDF of 15 Pa.C.S. §§ 1302 and 1306 (palegis.us; § 1302 at the same URL with sctn=002.), since the HTML view loads by script. Conditional items not quoted: § 1306(a)(4)(ii)-(iii) (share rights and board authority, to the extent determined or vested), (a)(6) term if not perpetual, (a)(7) delayed effective date. PA requires no registered agent name; § 109 lets a commercial registered office provider's name replace the address. Excerpts script-checked against the downloaded text.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more corporations for profit or not-for-profit or natural persons of full age may incorporate a business corporation under the provisions of this subpart.

items.text: Articles of incorporation shall be signed by each of the incorporators and shall set forth in the English language:
The name of the corporation, unless the name is in a foreign language in which case it shall be set forth in Roman letters or characters or Arabic or Roman numerals.

Subject to section 109 (relating to name of commercial registered office provider in lieu of registered address), the address, including street and number, if any, of its initial registered office in this Commonwealth.
A statement that the corporation is incorporated under the provisions of the Business Corporation Law of 1988.
A statement that the corporation is to be organized upon a nonstock basis, or if it is to be organized on a stock share basis:

The aggregate number of shares that the corporation shall have authority to issue. It shall not be necessary to set forth in the articles the designations of the classes of shares of the corporation, or the maximum number of shares of each class that may be issued.
The name of each of the incorporators.

jurisdictions.name: Rhode Island
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of State, UCC
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a president, secretary and treasurer; a registered agent in the state; an annual report each year ($50, due February 1 to May 1).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "corporation", "company", "incorporated", "limited" or an abbreviation; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Business corporation tax 7% flat of Rhode Island-apportioned net income (2026), with a $400 minimum.
jurisdictions.notes: Officers per R.I. Gen. Laws §7-1.2-812; annual report $50 per the Secretary of State costs-and-fees page (https://www.sos.ri.gov/divisions/business-services/business-basics/costs-and-fees). Whether one person may hold all offices was not confirmed. 7% rate confirmed for 2025 filings; no 2026 change found. Articles: Read from the official Rhode Island General Assembly statute pages (§ 201 at 7-1.2-201.htm).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals may act as incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by filing articles of incorporation for the corporation with the secretary of state.

items.text: The articles of incorporation must state:
A corporate name that satisfies the requirements of § 7-1.2-401.

The total number of shares which the corporation has authority to issue, and if the corporation is to be authorized to issue more than one class of shares: (i) The total number of shares of each class; and (ii) A statement of all or any of the designations and the powers, preferences, and rights, including voting rights, and the qualifications, limitations, or restrictions of them, …
The address of its initial registered office, and the name of its initial registered agent at the address.
The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Vermont
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC Liens
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; officers as the bylaws provide (one keeps minutes); a registered agent in the state; an annual report each year ($60).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "corporation", "incorporated", "company", "limited" or an abbreviation; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax in brackets (2026): 6% up to $10,000, 7% to $25,000, 8.5% above; minimum tax by Vermont gross receipts, from $100 up to $100,000.
jurisdictions.notes: Directors per 11A V.S.A. §8.03, officers per §8.40. Annual report fee $60 is from the current statute (§1.22); many third-party sites still show $45 (the 2013 fee). Minimum tax tiers ($100/$500/$2,000/$6,000/$100,000) come from a January 2026 legislative presentation, not tax.vermont.gov; the 2026 legislature studied corporate tax changes, none confirmed enacted. Articles: Read from the official Vermont Legislature statutes pages (§ 2.01 at .../00002.01). The official text uses a curly apostrophe in (a)(4).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more natural persons of majority age may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: The articles of incorporation shall set forth:
a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 4.01 of this title;
the classes of shares, if any, and the number of shares in each class that the corporation is authorized to issue;
the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
the street address of the corporation’s initial registered office and the name and email of its initial registered agent for service of process at that office pursuant to 11 V.S.A. § 1655;
the name and address of each incorporator;
one or more classes of shares that together have unlimited voting rights; and
one or more classes of shares, which may be the same class or classes as those with voting rights, that together are entitled to receive the net assets of the corporation upon dissolution.

jurisdictions.name: Illinois
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators. No residency or capital requirement. Officers as set by the bylaws, a registered agent and office in Illinois, and an annual report ($75 plus franchise tax).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include a word such as Corporation or Inc.; English letters and Arabic or Roman numerals are allowed.
jurisdictions.tax: For 2026, 9.5% on net income: 7% corporate income tax plus 2.5% personal property replacement tax. Franchise tax on paid-in capital, but the first $10,000 of liability is exempt.
jurisdictions.notes: The franchise tax exemption is $10,000 from 2025 under 805 ILCS 5/15.35, as read from a FindLaw copy because ilga.gov failed TLS. Bills to raise the 2026 exemption to $100,000 (HB 2846/2861) or repeal the tax (HB 5526) were not confirmed enacted. The $75 report fee comes from an SOS form and secondary sources. Officer rule (8.50) not confirmed. Articles: Read from the General Assembly's ILCS documents (2.05 at https://www.ilga.gov/Documents/legislation/ilcs/documents/080500050K2.05.htm). The ilga.gov server omits its intermediate TLS certificate; it was fetched from the issuer (Sectigo) so the download was still verified. Item (a)(6) is trimmed after its first sentence. Conditional items not quoted: (a)(7) class designations and rights if shares are divided into classes, (a)(8) series terms if preferred or special shares may be issued in series. Excerpts script-checked.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more incorporators may organize a corporation under this Act. Each incorporator shall be either a corporation, domestic or foreign, or a natural person of the age of 18 years or more.

items.text: The articles of incorporation must set forth:
a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of this Act;

the purpose or purposes for which the corporation is organized, which may be stated to be, or to include, the transaction of any or all lawful businesses for which corporations may be incorporated under this Act;
the address of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office;
the name and address of each incorporator;
the number of shares of each class the corporation is authorized to issue;

the number and class of shares which the corporation proposes to issue without further report to the Secretary of State, and the consideration to be received, less expenses, including commissions, paid or incurred in connection with the issuance of shares, by the corporation therefor.

jurisdictions.name: Indiana
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC filings and searches (INBiz)
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators. No residency or capital requirement. Officers as set by the bylaws, a registered agent in Indiana, and a business entity report every two years (about $31-32 online, $50 paper).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include a word such as Corporation or Inc.; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate adjusted gross income tax 4.9% flat (2026); no separate franchise tax.
jurisdictions.notes: The online report fee conflicts: the in.gov SOS page reportedly says $31 and INBiz says $32. The statutory fee is $20 electronic, plus an access fee. The officer rule (IC 23-1-36-1) and the name-statute citation were not fetched directly. Articles: The iga.in.gov code viewer renders by script, so the text was read from the General Assembly's official 2026 Indiana Code HTML download (https://iga.in.gov/ic/2026/2026-Indiana-Code-html.zip, Title 23). Excerpts script-checked against it.

who_may_incorporate.text: One (1) or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by causing the person's name to be listed on the articles of incorporation and having the articles of incorporation provided to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: The articles of incorporation must set forth:
a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of IC 23-1-23-1 (before its repeal) or IC 23-0.5-3;
the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
the street address of the corporation's initial registered office in Indiana and the name of its initial registered agent at that office; and
the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Iowa
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators. No residency or capital requirement. Officers as set by the bylaws, a registered agent in Iowa, and a biennial report in even-numbered years ($60 under statute).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include Corporation, Inc., Company or Ltd. and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax for 2026 is 5.5% on the first $100,000 and 7.1% above that, unchanged from 2024-2025 by Order 2025-02; 2027 is also unchanged.
jurisdictions.notes: The 2026 Iowa Code (490.122) lists a $60 biennial report fee. Some sources cite $45 paper and $30 online under an administrative rule, not confirmed on sos.iowa.gov. The report is due January 1 to April 1 of even-numbered years. The officer rule (490.840) was not fetched. Articles: Read from the Legislature's Iowa Code 2026 section PDFs (490.201 at https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/490.201.pdf). Excerpts script-checked against the PDF text.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: The articles of incorporation must set forth all of the following:
A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 490.401.
The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue.
The street and mailing addresses of the corporation’s initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office.
The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Kansas
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC filing information
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators. No residency or capital requirement. Officers as set by the bylaws, a registered agent in Kansas, and a biennial information report by April 15 ($90 online, $110 paper).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must be distinguishable on Secretary of State records; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax for 2026 is a 3.5% normal tax plus a 3% surtax on income over $50,000, so 6.5% at the top. No franchise tax.
jurisdictions.notes: The normal rate was cut from 4% to 3.5% under APEX from 2024 (Notice 23-10). The 2025 K-120 shows 3.5% + 3%. Notice 25-06 says no trigger cut for 2026, and Notice 26-11 says none for 2027. The 2026 form has not been seen. Many secondary sources still say 4%/7%. Report fees are from the IFP form, revised 7/22/26. Single sales factor apportionment starts in 2027. Articles: Kansas follows the Delaware model but calls the filing articles of incorporation. Read from the Legislature's 2026 Kansas Statutes pages (17-6001 at the matching 017_060_0001 URL). (a)(4)(A) is trimmed before its sentence on class designations and board authority, which applies only where fixing them in the articles is desired. Conditional items not quoted: (a)(4)(B) nonstock statement, (a)(6) initial directors if incorporators' powers end on filing. Excerpts script-checked.

who_may_incorporate.text: Any person, partnership, association or corporation, singly or jointly with others, and without regard to such person's or entity's residence, domicile or state of incorporation, may incorporate or organize a corporation under this code by filing with the secretary of state articles of incorporation which shall be executed and filed in accordance with K.S.A. 17-7908 through 17-7910, and amendments thereto.

items.text: The articles of incorporation shall set forth:
The name of the corporation pursuant to K.S.A. 17-7918 and 17-7919, and amendments thereto, of the business entity standard treatment act;
the postal address of the corporation's registered office in this state stated in accordance with K.S.A. 17-7924, and amendments thereto, and the name of its resident agent at such address;

the nature of the business or purposes to be conducted or promoted. It shall be sufficient to state, either alone or with other businesses or purposes, that the purpose of the corporation is to engage in any lawful act or activity for which corporations may be organized under the Kansas general corporation code, and by such statement all lawful acts and activities shall be within the purposes of the corporation, except for express limitations, if any;

if the corporation is to be authorized to issue only one class of stock, the total number of shares of stock that the corporation shall have authority to issue and the par value of each of such shares, or a statement that all such shares are to be without par value. If the corporation is to be authorized to issue more than one class of stock, the articles of incorporation shall set forth the total number of shares of all classes of stock that the corporation shall have authority to issue and the number of shares of each class, and shall specify each class the shares of which are to be without par value, and each class the shares of which are to have a par value and the par value of the shares of each such class.
the name and postal address of the incorporator or incorporators; and

jurisdictions.name: Michigan
jurisdictions.office: Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, Corporations Division
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one incorporator; no residency or capital requirement; a president, secretary and treasurer (one person may hold several); a registered agent in Michigan; an annual report by May 15 ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include a word such as Corporation or Inc. and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax 6% flat (2026). Corporations with under $350,000 of Michigan gross receipts, or liability of $100 or less, need not file or pay.
jurisdictions.notes: The michigan.gov CIT page returned 403 to the fetch, so the rate and threshold come from its search snippet. The rule that one person may hold several offices (MCL 450.1531) was taken from a secondary summary. Articles: Read from the Legislature's MCL pages (450.1201 at objectName=mcl-450-1201), current through PA 114 of 2026. (b) is trimmed: the omitted words introduce subparagraph (i) and the exceptions in (ii)-(iii) for educational and professional corporations. Conditional items not quoted: (d)-(e) class and series terms and board authority if shares are in classes or series, (h) duration if not perpetual. Excerpts script-checked.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may be the incorporators of a corporation by signing and filing articles of incorporation for the corporation.

items.text: The articles of incorporation shall contain all of the following:
The name of the corporation.

The purposes for which the corporation is formed. … it is a sufficient compliance with this subdivision to state substantially, alone or with specifically enumerated purposes, that the corporation may engage in any activity within the purposes for which corporations may be formed under the business corporation act, and all activities shall by the statement be considered within the purposes of the corporation, subject to expressed limitations.
The aggregate number of shares that the corporation has authority to issue.

Except as otherwise provided in section 611(2)(c), the street address, and the mailing address if different from the street address, of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of the corporation's initial resident agent at that address.
The names and addresses of the incorporators.

jurisdictions.name: Minnesota
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC forms and fees
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators. No residency or capital requirement. Needs a chief executive officer and a chief financial officer, a Minnesota registered office address, and a free annual renewal by December 31.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include Corporation, Incorporated or Limited (or Company) in English letters and be distinguishable; nothing provides for assigned numbered names.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate franchise (income) tax 9.8% flat for 2026, among the highest in the US, plus a graduated minimum fee based on Minnesota property, payroll and sales.
jurisdictions.notes: The 2026 Minnesota Statutes still show 9.8% (290.06 subd. 1, with no 2026 amendment). Bills to cut the rate were reported as not enacted. The $0 domestic renewal fee is from the SOS fee schedule and 302A.821. The minimum-fee thresholds are indexed yearly and were not confirmed. A registered agent is optional, but a registered office address is required. Articles: Read from the Revisor of Statutes pages (302A.105 at https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/302A.105). Minnesota allows a registered agent to be omitted ('if any'). Excerpts script-checked.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more natural persons of at least 18 years of age may act as incorporators of a corporation by filing with the secretary of state articles of incorporation for the corporation.

items.text: The articles of incorporation shall contain:
the name of the corporation;
the address of the registered office of the corporation and the name of its registered agent, if any, at that address;
the aggregate number of shares that the corporation has authority to issue; and
the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Missouri
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one incorporator (an adult individual); a president and a secretary (one person may hold both); no residency or capital requirement; a Missouri registered agent; an annual report each year ($20 online).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "corporation", "company", "incorporated" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax 4% flat (2026, unchanged since 2020); the corporate franchise tax was repealed from 2016.
jurisdictions.notes: Officers per RSMo 351.360, incorporator per 351.050. The $20 online fee ($45 paper) comes from third-party guides; the Secretary of State's page only says online filing saves $25. The DOR page found no 2026 change; bills to phase out the corporate income tax were not confirmed as enacted. Articles: Read from revisor.mo.gov (351.055 effective 28 Aug 2004; 351.050 at https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=351.050). Item (3) is trimmed; it applies only above 30,000 shares or $30,000 par value and also requires a statement of class preferences and rights. Missouri, unlike MBCA states, still requires duration and purposes.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more natural persons of the age of eighteen years, or more, may act as an incorporator of such corporation by signing and delivering in the office of the secretary of state the articles of incorporation of such corporation.

items.text: The name of the corporation;
The address, including street and number, if any, of its initial registered office in this state, and the name of its initial registered agent at such address;

If the aggregate number of shares which the corporation shall have the authority to issue exceeds thirty thousand shares or the par value exceeds thirty thousand dollars the corporation shall indicate the number of shares of each class, if any, that are to have a par value and the par value of each share of each such class, and the number of shares of each class, if any, that are to be without par value …
The name and physical business or residence address of each incorporator;
The number of years the corporation is to continue, which may be any number or perpetual;
The purposes for which the corporation is formed.

jurisdictions.name: Nebraska
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one incorporator; officers per the bylaws (one person may hold all); no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Nebraska; a biennial occupation tax report in even years (from $26, by paid-up capital).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable on the records; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax 4.55% flat on all Nebraska taxable income (tax years beginning in 2026), down from 5.20% in 2025 and scheduled to fall to 3.99% in 2027.
jurisdictions.notes: The 2026 rate is confirmed by the Department of Revenue's Revenue Sources 2025 report; some secondary sites wrongly list 5.20% for 2026. The domestic occupation tax runs from $26 to $23,990 by paid-up capital stock, due March 1 of even years and delinquent after April 15. Directors per Neb. Rev. Stat. 21-286 and officers per 21-2,105 were read via Justia's 2023 text, not the Legislature's current text. Articles: Read from nebraskalegislature.gov (21-219 at https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=21-219). Omitted 21-220(a)(5), which applies only to a corporation registered as an investment company that limits annual shareholder meetings. Nebraska, unusually, requires par value in the articles.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 21-230;

The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue and, if such shares are to consist of one class only, the par value of each of such shares or, if such shares are to be divided into classes, the number of shares of each class and a statement of the par value of the shares of each such class;

The street address of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office. A post office box number may be provided in addition to the street address;
The name and address of each incorporator; and

jurisdictions.name: North Dakota
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Lien Filings / UCC
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators (adults); a president, secretary and treasurer (one person may hold all); no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent; an annual report each year ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "company", "corporation", "incorporated" or "limited" (or an abbreviation), use ASCII characters and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate income tax in brackets for 2026: 1.41% up to $25,000, 3.55% to $50,000 and 4.31% top rate above that (unchanged since 2015); a 3.5% surtax applies to water's-edge filers.
jurisdictions.notes: N.D.C.C. 10-19.1-33 (directors), -09 (incorporators), -52 and -55 (officers), -13 (name), -146 and -147 (annual report, $25). A domestic corporation's annual report is due before August 2 each year. The tax page says the rates are unchanged since 2015 and does not name 2026 explicitly. Articles: Read from the official chapter PDF on ndlegis.gov; the excerpts were checked against text extracted with pdftotext. Omitted 10-19.1-10(1)(f), which applies only if the filer wants an effective date later than the date the certificate is issued (at most 90 days later).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals of the age of eighteen years or more may act as incorporators of a corporation by filing with the secretary of state articles of incorporation for the corporation.

items.text: The name of the corporation.
The name of the registered agent as provided in chapter 10-01.1 and, if a noncommercial registered agent, then the address of that noncommercial registered agent in this state.
The address of the principal executive office.
The aggregate number of shares that the corporation has authority to issue.
The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Ohio
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators (any person, regardless of residence); a president, secretary and treasurer (one person may hold several); no capital requirement; an Ohio statutory agent; no annual report.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include "company", "corporation", "incorporated" or an abbreviation and be distinguishable on the records; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: No corporate income tax; the Commercial Activity Tax (gross receipts) is 0.26% on receipts above a $6 million annual exclusion (2025 and later, so 2026). The annual minimum tax was eliminated from 2024.
jurisdictions.notes: codes.ohio.gov refused connections, so the statutes were read through search excerpts. R.C. 1701.56 has set a one-director minimum since 2012; the old three-director rule appears only in outdated sources. Officers per 1701.64; name words per 1701.05 come from a secondary summary. The no-annual-report rule is from ohiosos.gov pages, with only professional associations and LLPs filing biennially. HB 96 (2025) changed no CAT rate or exclusion, per a secondary source. Articles: NOT read from the official site: codes.ohio.gov refused or timed out every connection (curl and WebFetch), as did the legislature's LIS host. Text comes from the casemine.com copy (https://www.casemine.com/act/us/645dc90fdc967037b33de925), which reflects amendments through the 133rd General Assembly (2021). The current official version is dated 9/30/2025 (HB 96) and could not be compared, so the wording may differ. Division (C) separately requires a written statutory-agent appointment to be filed with the articles.

who_may_incorporate.text: Any person, singly or jointly with others, and without regard to residence, domicile, or state of incorporation, may form a corporation by signing and filing with the secretary of state articles of incorporation that shall set forth all of the following:

items.text: The name of the corporation, which shall be in compliance with division (A) of section 1701.05 of the Revised Code;
The place in this state where the principal office of the corporation is to be located;

The authorized number and the par value per share of shares with par value, and the authorized number of shares without par value, except that the articles of a banking, safe deposit, trust, or insurance corporation shall not authorize shares without par value; the express terms, if any, of the shares; and, if the shares are classified, the designation of each class, the authorized number and par value per share, if any, of the shares of each class, and the express terms of the shares of each class;
If the corporation is to have an initial stated capital, the amount of that stated capital.

jurisdictions.name: South Dakota
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC filing
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one incorporator; officers per the bylaws, one keeping records; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in South Dakota; an annual report each year ($55 online).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company" or "limited" (or an abbreviation); numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: No corporate income tax (2026); only banks and financial institutions pay a bank franchise tax. South Dakota also has no personal income tax.
jurisdictions.notes: The annual report fee rose from $50 to $55 online on July 1, 2025 ($70 on paper), per the Secretary of State's fee schedule (https://sdsos.gov/general-information/filing-fees.aspx). It is due on the first day of the anniversary month, with a $55 late fee. SDCL 47-1A-201 covers incorporators and 47-1A-840 officers. The fetched part of 47-1A-401 did not show the distinguishability rule. Articles: Read from the sdlegislature.gov statute API (https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/47-1A-202.html and .../47-1A-201.html), which serves the official text behind the JavaScript page. Item (4) points to SDCL § 59-11-6 (registered agent information, in the Uniform Registered Agent Act), which was not quoted here.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Office of the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of §§ 47-1A-401 to 47-1A-401.3, inclusive;
The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
The street address of its principal office;
The information required by § 59-11-6; and
The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Wisconsin
jurisdictions.office: Department of Financial Institutions, Corporations Bureau
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of Financial Institutions, UCC
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (individuals) and one or more incorporators; officers as set by the bylaws; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Wisconsin; an annual report each year, filed online ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable on DFI records; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Corporate franchise/income tax 7.9% flat (2026); a manufacturing and agriculture credit can sharply reduce tax on qualifying income.
jurisdictions.notes:
DFI's fee schedule (effective April 17, 2022; https://wdfi.org/corporations/fees/us.htm) lists the stock-corporation annual report at $25 electronic or $40 paper; domestic corporations must file online. The report is due by the end of the quarter of the anniversary. Incorporators (180.0201) and officers (180.0840) were not fetched. The name statute was read from search excerpts after a rate limit. The 7.9% rate (s. 71.27) is confirmed by statute excerpts; no 2026 change was found. Articles: Read from docs.legis.wisconsin.gov. Omitted these conditional items:
- 180.0202(1)(d)3: class preferences, before shares of a class are issued.
- (1)(e): series terms.
- (1)(f): any provision letting the board act under s. 180.0602(1).
- (1)(g): any provision granting or limiting preemptive rights.
Unusually, Wisconsin requires the registered agent's e-mail address.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation.

items.text: A statement that the corporation is incorporated under this chapter.
A corporate name that satisfies s. 180.0401.
The number of authorized shares, except that an investment company may declare an indefinite number of authorized shares.
If more than one class of shares is authorized, all of the following:
The distinguishing designation of each class.
The number of shares of each class that the corporation is authorized to issue, except that an investment company may declare that each class has an indefinite number of authorized shares.
The street address of the corporation’s initial registered office and the name and e-mail address of its initial registered agent at that office.
The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Alabama
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC Records
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Alabama; a yearly business privilege tax return and annual report to Revenue, not required if the tax would be $100 or less.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name and must reserve it with the Secretary of State before filing the certificate of formation; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 6.5% corporate income tax (federal income tax deductible), plus business privilege tax of $0.25 to $1.75 per $1,000 of Alabama net worth (maximum $15,000); no minimum tax.
jurisdictions.notes: Alabama has no Secretary of State annual report; Form CPT is the 'Business Privilege Tax Return and Annual Report'. The TY2026 quick reference says taxpayers who would owe the $100 minimum have no filing requirement. The mandatory name reservation rule (Ala. Code 10A-1-5.10) is from SOS guidance and secondary summaries; the statute text was not read directly. Articles: Read on the official ALISON site (Alabama Legislature) in a browser; text saved and checked by script against that capture. Who-may-incorporate text is from https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/code-of-alabama?section=10A-2A-2.01. The section lists no separate filing-form items; the general certificate-of-formation rule in § 10A-1-3.05 is expressly displaced. Citation history shows amendment by Act 2026-495.

who_may_incorporate.text: In order to incorporate a corporation, one or more incorporators must execute a certificate of incorporation and deliver it for filing to the Secretary of State.

items.text: (1) a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of Article 5 of Chapter 1;
(2) the number of shares of stock the corporation is authorized to issue;

(3) the street and mailing addresses of the corporation’s initial registered office, the county within this state in which the street and mailing address is located, and the name of the corporation’s initial registered agent at that office as required by Article 5 of Chapter 1; and
(4) the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Arkansas
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of State, Business and Commercial Services
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Arkansas; an annual franchise tax report due May 1 (minimum $150 for corporations with stock).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable on the register; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: graduated corporate income tax of 1% to 4.3% (4.3% on income over $11,000), with the top rate cut to 4.1% from 2027; plus annual franchise tax of 0.3% of outstanding capital stock, minimum $150.
jurisdictions.notes: The 2026 special-session cut (signed May 6, 2026) lowers the top corporate rate to 4.1% from January 1, 2027; 2026 stays at 4.3%. The rate is confirmed by the Arkansas Economic Development Commission and Tax Foundation, not a DFA page. Franchise tax figures come from the Secretary of State's 2020 form; corporations without stock pay $300. The name statute was amended by Act 256 of 2023; the current text was not read. Articles: Not read from the official LexisNexis public site: Lexis served a CAPTCHA on document access for Georgia, so the other Lexis-hosted codes were not tried. Text taken from Justia's 2025 Arkansas Code (unofficial copy), captured in a browser and checked by script against that capture; Justia flattens paragraph breaks. § 4-27-201 from https://law.justia.com/codes/arkansas/title-4/subtitle-3/chapter-27/subchapter-2/section-4-27-201/. Item (3) incorporates § 4-20-105(a) (registered agent information under the Model Registered Agents Act), not quoted here.

who_may_incorporate.text: (a) One (1) or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing. (b) One (1) or more natural persons who are between the ages of sixteen (16) and eighteen (18) years of age shall have a person who is at least twenty-one (21) years of age or older to serve on his or her behalf as an incorporator of a corporation by executing and filing according to § 4-27-120 articles of incorporation for the corporation.

items.text: (1) a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of § 4-27-401;

(2) the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue and, if such shares are to consist of one (1) class only, the par value of each of such shares, or a statement that all of such shares are without par value;
(3) the information required by § 4-20-105(a);
(4) the name and address of each incorporator; and

(5) the primary purpose or purposes for which the corporation is organized, which is provided to the Secretary of State for informational purposes and shall not, unless specifically stated in the articles of incorporation, limit the broad purposes provided in § 4-27-301.

jurisdictions.name: Delaware
jurisdictions.office: Department of State, Division of Corporations
jurisdictions.security_registry: Division of Corporations, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Delaware; an annual franchise tax report due March 1 ($50 filing fee plus franchise tax).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include a word such as 'Corporation', 'Company', 'Incorporated' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation); numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: 8.7% income tax only on corporations doing business in Delaware; those merely keeping a registered office there are exempt. All pay franchise tax: $175 minimum (authorized shares) or $400 (assumed par), up to $200,000.
jurisdictions.notes: The income tax exemption for corporations that do no business in Delaware is 30 Del. C. 1902(b)(6); holding companies managing intangible investments may be exempt under 1902(b)(8). Large Corporate Filers pay up to $250,000 in franchise tax. Delaware also levies a gross receipts tax on Delaware business activity, not covered here. Board size (8 Del. C. 141(b)) comes from the statute and was not re-read. Articles: Read from the official Delaware Code Online. Paragraph (6) applies only if the incorporators' powers end on filing. Paragraph (4) is trimmed; its omitted text covers class designations and nonstock corporations.

who_may_incorporate.text: Any person, partnership, association or corporation, singly or jointly with others, and without regard to such person’s or entity’s residence, domicile or state of incorporation, may incorporate or organize a corporation under this chapter by filing with the Division of Corporations in the Department of State a certificate of incorporation which shall be executed, acknowledged and filed in accordance with § 103 of this title.

items.text: (1) The name of the corporation, which (i) shall contain 1 of the words “association,” “company,” “corporation,” “club,” “foundation,” “fund,” “incorporated,” “institute,” “society,” “union,” “syndicate,” or “limited,” (or abbreviations thereof, with or without punctuation), or words (or abbreviations thereof, with or without punctuation) of like import of foreign countries or jurisdictions (provided they are written in roman characters or letters); …
(2) The address (which shall be stated in accordance with § 131(c) of this title) of the corporation’s registered office in this State, and the name of its registered agent at such address;
(3) The nature of the business or purposes to be conducted or promoted. …

(4) If the corporation is to be authorized to issue only 1 class of stock, the total number of shares of stock which the corporation shall have authority to issue and the par value of each of such shares, or a statement that all such shares are to be without par value. If the corporation is to be authorized to issue more than 1 class of stock, the certificate of incorporation shall set forth the total number of shares of all classes of stock which the corporation shall have authority to issue and the number of shares of each class and shall specify each class the shares of which are to be without par value and each class the shares of which are to have par value and the par value of the shares of each such class. …
(5) The name and mailing address of the incorporator or incorporators;

(6) If the powers of the incorporator or incorporators are to terminate upon the filing of the certificate of incorporation, the names and mailing addresses of the persons who are to serve as directors until the first annual meeting of stockholders or until their successors are elected and qualify.

jurisdictions.name: Florida
jurisdictions.office: Department of State, Division of Corporations (Sunbiz)
jurisdictions.security_registry: Florida Secured Transaction Registry
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Florida; an annual report each year by May 1 ($150; a $400 late fee).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Company' or 'Incorporated' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable on the register; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 5.5% corporate income tax on Florida net income, with the first $50,000 exempt; no franchise or net-worth tax.
jurisdictions.notes: The DOR page lists 5.5% for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2022, and the $50,000 exemption. No 2026 change was found. Articles: Read from The 2026 Florida Statutes on the Legislature's site; s. 607.0201 from the same site (URL ...Sections/0607.0201.html).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the department for filing.

items.text: (a) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of s. 607.0401;
(b) The street address of the initial principal office and, if different, the mailing address of the corporation;
(c) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(d) The street address of the corporation’s initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office together with a written acceptance as required in s. 607.0501(3); and
