jurisdictions.name: Georgia
jurisdictions.security_registry: Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority, UCC System (filed with any county clerk)
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Georgia; newspaper notice of incorporation; an annual registration by April 1 ($50 state fee) naming the CEO, CFO and secretary.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable on the register; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 4.99% corporate income tax (down from 5.19% in 2025), with further cuts of 0.125 points a year possible, down to 3.99%, if revenue targets are met.
jurisdictions.notes: The Georgia DOR page says only that the income tax rate is a flat 4.99% for 2026, without saying 'corporate'. BDO's summary of H.B. 463 says it covers both individual and corporate rates. Some sites still show 5.19%. Secondary sources give the annual registration total as $60 including a $10 service fee. The name-statute URL follows Justia's pattern and was not opened. Articles: Not read from the official LexisNexis public site (reached via legis.ga.gov): opening the section triggered a CAPTCHA, which was not attempted. Text taken from Justia's 2025 Georgia Code (the version labelled effective July 1, 2026, after HB 1185, which changed only optional items in (b)), captured in a browser and checked by script against that capture. The Lexis search snippet for 14-2-202 matched the (a) wording. § 14-2-201 from https://law.justia.com/codes/georgia/title-14/chapter-2/article-2/section-14-2-201/. Separately, O.C.G.A. § 14-2-201.1 requires newspaper publication of a notice of incorporation (not an articles item).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of Code Section 14-2-401;
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(3) The street address and county of the corporation’s initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office;
(4) The name and address of each incorporator; and
(5) The mailing address of the initial principal office of the corporation, if different from the initial registered office.

jurisdictions.name: Kentucky
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Kentucky; an annual report between January 1 and June 30 ($15).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must be distinguishable from names on record and carry a corporate ending such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or 'Company'; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 5% corporate income tax, plus the limited liability entity tax (the lesser of 0.095% of Kentucky gross receipts or 0.75% of gross profits; $175 minimum), which is largely credited against the income tax.
jurisdictions.notes: The $15 annual report fee was confirmed by several secondary sources, not a Secretary of State page; a veteran-owned waiver exists. transparency.ky.gov still shows the pre-2018 graduated rates (4%/5%/6%); the Department of Revenue says the current rate is a flat 5%. The exact corporate endings in KRS 14A.3-010 are from secondary summaries. Articles: Read from the official KRS PDFs on the Kentucky Legislature site (KRS 271B.2-010 at statute.aspx?id=13317). Text extracted with pdftotext; line breaks normalized. Public benefit corporations must also state the items in KRS 271B.2-020(4).

who_may_incorporate.text: One (1) or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: (a) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of KRS 14A.3-010;
(b) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(c) The corporation's initial registered office and initial registered agent that satisfy the requirements of KRS 14A.4-010;
(d) The mailing address of the corporation's principal office; and
(e) The name and mailing address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Louisiana
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, File Financing Statements (filed with any parish clerk)
jurisdictions.legal_system: Mixed: civil law (the Louisiana Civil Code) for private law, with common-law influence; business corporation law is statutory and modeled on the Model Business Corporation Act.
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered office and at least one registered agent in Louisiana; an annual report each year ($35 from October 1, 2026).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must carry a corporate ending, be distinguishable and use English letters or characters; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 5.5% corporate income tax (since 2025), and the corporation franchise tax is repealed for periods beginning on or after January 1, 2026.
jurisdictions.notes: The annual report fee rose from $30 to $35 on October 1, 2026, under Act 921 of the 2026 Regular Session. The flat 5.5% rate (H.B. 2) and franchise tax repeal (H.B. 3) come from the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session; they are confirmed by practitioner summaries, not a Louisiana Department of Revenue page. Scholars debate whether Louisiana is best called 'mixed' or 'civilian'. Articles: Read from the Louisiana State Legislature's site (R.S. 12:1-201 at Law.aspx?d=920204). Item (A)(5) applies only if the corporation rejects or limits R.S. 12:1-832 protection. Note: R.S. 12:1-201 refers to the agent's consent as required by 'R.S. 12:1-202(E)', but in the current text the consent requirement is subsection (F).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons capable of contracting may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering to the secretary of state for filing articles of incorporation and the written consent of the registered agent required by R.S. 12:1-202(E).

items.text: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of R.S. 12:1-401.
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue.

(3) The street address, not a post office box only, of the corporation's initial registered office, and, if different, the street address, not a post office box only, of the corporation's initial principal office.
(4) The name and street address, not a post office box only, of its initial registered agent.
(5) If the corporation chooses to reject or limit the protection against liability of directors and officers that is provided by R.S. 12:1-832, a statement of the rejection or limitation.
(6) The name and address of each incorporator.
F. A written consent to appointment, signed by the initial registered agent, shall be attached or appended to the articles of incorporation.

jurisdictions.name: Maryland
jurisdictions.office: State Department of Assessments and Taxation, Business Entities
jurisdictions.security_registry: State Department of Assessments and Taxation, UCC filings
jurisdictions.minimums: At least one director and one or more adult incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; required officers are a president, secretary and treasurer; a resident agent in Maryland; an annual report by April 15 ($300).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 8.25% corporate income tax on Maryland taxable income; no separate franchise tax beyond the $300 annual report fee.
jurisdictions.notes: The minimum of one director is from Corps. & Ass'ns 2-402. The $300 fee is from SDAT's 2024 Form 1 and instructions. The naming rules are in Title 1, Subtitle 5, which 2-106 cross-references; the required words were not read directly. Articles: Read from the Maryland General Assembly's statute pages (§ 2-102 at ...section=2-102...). The site uses an en dash in section numbers (§2–104). Item (a)(7) (class descriptions) applies only if the stock is divided into classes and is omitted here.

who_may_incorporate.text: (a) Except as provided elsewhere in this section, in order to form a corporation, one or more adult individuals acting as incorporators shall: (1) Sign and acknowledge articles of incorporation; and (2) File them for record with the Department.

items.text: (1) The name and address of each incorporator and a statement that each incorporator is: (i) 18 years old or older; and (ii) Forming a corporation under the general laws of the State of Maryland;
(2) The name of the corporation;
(3) The purposes for which the corporation is formed or a statement that the corporation may engage in any lawful business or other activity;
(4) The address of the principal office of the corporation;
(5) The name and address of the resident agent of the corporation;

(6) (i) The total number of shares of stock of all classes which the corporation has authority to issue; (ii) The number of shares of stock of each class; (iii) The par value of the shares of stock of each class or a statement that the shares are without par value; and (iv) If there are any shares of stock with par value, the aggregate par value of all the shares of all classes;
(8) The number of directors and the names of those individuals who will serve as directors until their successors are elected and qualify.

jurisdictions.name: Mississippi
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Mississippi; an annual report filed online by April 15 ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must carry a corporate designator such as 'Corporation' or 'Inc.' and be distinguishable on the register; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: graduated corporate income tax of 0% on the first $5,000, 4% on the next $5,000 and 5% above $10,000. The franchise tax is phasing out: $0.50 per $1,000 of capital for 2026, $0.25 for 2027.
jurisdictions.notes: Sources conflict on the corporate rate. Some (Swanson Reed, a Tax Foundation narrative line) say it fell to 4% in 2026, but the DOR FAQ and Tax Foundation's rate data as of July 1, 2026 both show 4%/5% brackets; the cut to 4% appears to be the individual rate. Franchise tax: $25 minimum, applied to capital over $100,000; secondary sources say it is fully repealed from 2028. The $25 annual report fee is from secondary sources. Articles: Not read from the official LexisNexis public site: Lexis served a CAPTCHA on document access for Georgia, so the other Lexis-hosted codes were not tried. Text taken from Justia's 2025 Mississippi Code (unofficial copy), captured in a browser and checked by script against that capture. § 79-4-2.01 from https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-79/chapter-4/article-2/section-79-4-2-01/.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of Section 79-4-4.01;
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue and any information concerning the authorized shares as required by Section 79-4-6.01;
(3) The street address of the corporation’s initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office; and
(4) The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: North Carolina
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in North Carolina; an annual report each year ($25 on paper, $21 online).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 2% corporate income tax (2.25% in 2025), scheduled to reach 0% after 2029; plus franchise tax of $1.50 per $1,000 of tax base, $200 minimum and $500 maximum on the first $1 million.
jurisdictions.notes: The phase-down per G.S. 105-130.3: 2% for 2026 and 2027, 1% for 2028 and 2029, 0% after 2029. The $21 online fee includes a $3 card fee. The name-statute URL (G.S. 55D-20) follows the legislature's pattern and was not opened. Articles: Not read from the official site: ncleg.gov returned a Cloudflare block to both scripted and browser requests. Text taken from Justia's 2025 North Carolina General Statutes (history through S.L. 2025-33), captured in a browser and checked by script against that capture. § 55-2-01 from https://law.justia.com/codes/north-carolina/chapter-55/article-2/section-55-2-01/.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of G.S. 55D-20 and G.S. 55D-21;
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue and any other information required by G.S. 55-6-01;

(3) The street address, and the mailing address if different from the street address, of the corporation's initial registered office, the county in which the initial registered office is located, and the name of the corporation's initial registered agent at that address;

(4) The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma
jurisdictions.security_registry: Oklahoma County Clerk, the central UCC filing office
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Oklahoma; no annual report for domestic corporations since the franchise tax was repealed.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must include a word such as 'Corporation', 'Company', 'Incorporated' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation); numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 4% corporate income tax; the franchise tax was repealed from tax year 2024 (2023 was the last return).
jurisdictions.notes: That domestic corporations have no annual report is confirmed only by secondary sources (Harbor Compliance, Northwest Registered Agent); no Secretary of State page was found. The 4% rate (68 O.S. 2355) is from secondary sources and Tax Foundation's 2026 index. 2025 bills to end the corporate income tax (SB 292, SB 322) were not shown as enacted. The name-statute URL follows Justia's pattern and was not opened. Articles: Read from OSCN (Oklahoma State Courts Network), which hosts the Oklahoma Statutes; it is not the Legislature's own site. § 1005 is at DeliverDocument.asp?CiteID=67011. 'Section 7 of this act' in § 1005 means 18 O.S. § 1007. Paragraphs 7 and 8 of § 1006(A) apply only to not-for-profit and charitable nonstock corporations and are omitted; paragraph 6 applies only if the incorporators' powers end on filing. Long paragraphs are trimmed.

who_may_incorporate.text: A. Any person, partnership, association or corporation, singly or jointly with others, and without regard to his or their residence, domicile or state of incorporation, may incorporate or organize a corporation pursuant to the provisions of the Oklahoma General Corporation Act by filing with the Secretary of State a certificate of incorporation which shall be executed, acknowledged and filed in accordance with the provisions of Section 7 of this act …

items.text: 1. The name of the corporation which shall contain one of the words “association”, “company”, “corporation”, “club”, “foundation”, “fund”, “incorporated”, “institute”, “society”, “union”, “syndicate”, or “limited” or abbreviations thereof, with or without punctuation, or words or abbreviations thereof, with or without punctuation, of like import of foreign countries or jurisdictions; provided that such abbreviations are written in Roman characters or letters, …
2. The address including the street, number, city and postal code of the corporation’s registered office in this state, and the name of the corporation’s registered agent at such address;
3. The nature of the business or purposes to be conducted or promoted. …

4. If the corporation is to be authorized to issue only one class of stock, the total number of shares of stock which the corporation shall have authority to issue and the par value of each of such shares, or a statement that all such shares are to be without par value. …
5. The name and mailing address of the incorporator or incorporators;

6. If the powers of the incorporator or incorporators are to terminate upon the filing of the certificate of incorporation, the names and mailing addresses of the persons who are to serve as directors until the first annual meeting of shareholders or until their successors are elected and qualify;

jurisdictions.name: South Carolina
jurisdictions.act: South Carolina Business Corporation Act of 1988
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; the articles need a certificate signed by a South Carolina-licensed attorney; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in the state; an annual report filed with the SC1120 return.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 5% corporate income tax, plus an annual license fee of 0.1% of capital and paid-in surplus plus $15 (minimum $25), paid with the annual report.
jurisdictions.notes: The initial annual report (CL-1) and a $25 initial license fee go with the articles. Later annual reports are Schedule D of the SC1120 return, filed with the Department of Revenue by the 15th day of the fourth month after year end. Articles: Read from the South Carolina Legislature's Code of Laws. Under § 33-2-102(d) the articles must also be accompanied by the initial annual report (§ 12-20-40); that is a filing attachment, not part of the articles' contents.

who_may_incorporate.text: Any person may act as the incorporator of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: (1) a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of Section 33-4-101;
(2) the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue, itemized by classes;
(3) the street address of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office;
(4) the name and address of each incorporator;
(5) the signature of each incorporator; and
(6) a certificate, signed by an attorney licensed to practice in this State, that all of the requirements of this section have been complied with.

jurisdictions.name: Tennessee
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, business and UCC services
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Tennessee; an annual report each year ($20) listing at least one officer.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or 'Company' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: 6.5% excise tax on net earnings plus franchise tax of 0.25% of net worth ($100 minimum); the property-based franchise measure was repealed in 2024. No personal income tax on wages.
jurisdictions.notes: The 6.5% excise rate (Tenn. Code 67-4-2007) is well established, but no fetched official page stated it. A 2025 proposal (SB0037) to raise the corporate annual report fee to $300 was reportedly withdrawn; its status is unconfirmed. The SOS FAQ was quoted via search because direct fetch was blocked. Articles: Not read from the official LexisNexis public site: Lexis served a CAPTCHA on document access for Georgia, so the other Lexis-hosted codes were not tried. Text taken from Justia's 2025 Tennessee Code (unofficial copy), captured in a browser and checked by script against that capture. § 48-12-101 from https://law.justia.com/codes/tennessee/title-48/for-profit-business-corporations/chapter-12/section-48-12-101/. Item (a)(6) incorporates Chapter 16 (shares), not quoted here.

who_may_incorporate.text: One (1) or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering a charter to the secretary of state for filing. …

items.text: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of § 48-14-101;
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;

(3) The street address and zip code of the corporation's initial registered office (and a mailing address such as a post office box if the United States postal service does not deliver to the registered agent's registered office), the county in which the office is located, and the name of its initial registered agent at that office;
(4) The name and address and zip code of each incorporator;

(5) The street address and zip code of the initial principal office of the corporation (and a mailing address such as a post office box if the United States postal service does not deliver to the principal office);
(6) Information required by chapter 16 of this title; and
(7) A statement that the corporation is for profit.

jurisdictions.name: Texas
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of State, Business and Public Filings
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and organizers; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Texas; no Secretary of State annual report, but a franchise tax report or Public Information Report to the Comptroller each May 15.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Company' or 'Incorporated' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: No corporate income tax. 2026 franchise (margin) tax: 0.75% of taxable margin (0.375% retail or wholesale; 0.331% EZ rate up to $20 million revenue); no tax due at or below $2.65 million revenue.
jurisdictions.notes: The no-tax-due threshold rose from $2.47 million (2024 and 2025 reports) to $2.65 million for 2026 and 2027 reports; some sites still show $2.47 million. Entities under the threshold still file a Public Information Report or Ownership Information Report. Articles: Read from the Texas Legislature's statutes site (tcss.legis.texas.gov; statutes.capitol.texas.gov now serves a script-only shell). Omitted conditional items: § 3.005(a)(4) (fixed duration), (a)(7)(B)-(C) (limited partnerships and REITs), (a)(8) (conversion or merger), (a)(9) (other code requirements); § 3.007(a)(4) (management by shareholders' agreement), (b) (multiple share classes) and (c) (preemptive or cumulative voting). Under § 3.004(b) each organizer must also sign the certificate.

who_may_incorporate.text: (a) Any person having the capacity to contract for the person or for another may be an organizer of a filing entity.

items.text: (1) the name of the filing entity being formed;
(2) the type of filing entity being formed;

(3) for filing entities other than limited partnerships, the purpose or purposes for which the filing entity is formed, which may be stated to be or include any lawful purpose for that type of entity;
(5) the street address of the initial registered office of the filing entity and the name of the initial registered agent of the filing entity at the office;
(6) the initial mailing address of the filing entity;
(7) the name and address of each: (A) organizer for the filing entity, unless the entity is formed under a plan of conversion or merger;
(1) the aggregate number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(2) if the shares the corporation is authorized to issue consist of one class of shares only, the par value of each share or a statement that each share is without par value;

(3) if the corporation is to be managed by a board of directors, the number of directors constituting the initial board of directors and the name and address of each individual who will serve as director until the first annual meeting of shareholders and until a successor is elected and qualified; and

jurisdictions.name: Virginia
jurisdictions.security_registry: State Corporation Commission, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no capital requirement; the registered agent must be a Virginia-resident officer, director or lawyer, or an authorized entity; a free annual report plus an annual registration fee from $100.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 6% corporate income tax on Virginia taxable income; no franchise tax beyond the SCC annual registration fee ($100 for up to 5,000 authorized shares).
jurisdictions.notes: The registration fee rises with authorized shares; secondary sources say it reaches a $1,700 maximum. The registered-agent qualifications come from Va. Code 13.1-634 and were not separately fetched. The name-statute URL follows the LIS pattern and was not opened. Articles: Read from the Virginia General Assembly's LIS Code of Virginia (§ 13.1-618 at .../section13.1-618/). Virginia's mandatory list has no incorporator name or address item. Item A.3 applies only if more than one class or series is authorized. The incorporator must sign the articles under § 13.1-618.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by signing and delivering articles of incorporation to the Commission for filing.

items.text: 1. A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of § 13.1-630;
2. The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
3. If more than one class or series of shares is authorized, the number of authorized shares of each class or series and a distinguishing designation for each class or series; and

4. The address of the corporation's initial registered office (including both (i) the post-office address with street and number, if any, and (ii) the name of the city or county in which it is located), and the name of its initial registered agent at that office, and that the agent is either (a) an individual who is a resident of Virginia and is designated as a director of the corporation in the initial articles of incorporation or a member of the Virginia State Bar or (b) a domestic or foreign stock or nonstock corporation, limited liability company, or registered limited liability partnership authorized to transact business in the Commonwealth.

jurisdictions.name: West Virginia
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of State, Business and Licensing
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and incorporators; no residency or capital requirement; an in-state registered agent is optional (the Secretary of State accepts service of process); an annual report by June 30 ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company' or 'Limited' (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Tax year 2026: flat 6.5% corporate net income tax; no separate business franchise tax.
jurisdictions.notes: W. Va. Code 31D-5-501 says a corporation 'may' keep a registered office and agent. The Secretary of State's role as attorney-in-fact for service is reflected in 2026 bill text and is not otherwise confirmed. The 6.5% rate is from the 2025 CIT-120 instructions. 2026 bills SB 397 (halve the rate) and SB 735 (phase out from 2027) were not shown as enacted. The 2015 repeal of the business franchise tax is from general knowledge. Articles: Read from the West Virginia Legislature's Code site (§31D-2-201 at https://code.wvlegislature.gov/31D-2-201/). The registered office and agent are required only 'if any', consistent with § 31D-5-501 making them optional.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the Secretary of State for filing.

items.text: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section four hundred one, article four of this chapter;
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue, the par value of each of the shares or a statement that all shares are without par value;
(3) The street address of the corporation's initial registered office, if any, and the name of its initial registered agent at that office, if any;

jurisdictions.name: Alaska
jurisdictions.office: Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of Natural Resources, Recorder's Office, UCC Central File
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (three if the articles and bylaws are silent) and one or more incorporators aged 18+; a president, secretary and treasurer; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Alaska; a biennial report ($100).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "company", "incorporated" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable on the register; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Graduated corporate net income tax for tax year 2026: 0% on the first $25,000 of taxable income, rising through ten brackets to a top rate of 9.4% on income above $222,000.
jurisdictions.notes: Minimums and name rules are from the Division of Corporations' statute compilation (rev. 6/26/2026): AS 10.06.453, .205, .483, .150, .845 and .105. The president and secretary must be different people unless one person owns all the shares. The tax brackets come from Tax Foundation's 2025 table, because tax.alaska.gov returned an error page. The 0%-9.4% range matches Alaska Department of Revenue reports. The brackets are fixed in AS 43.20.011(e) and not indexed, but I did not confirm them against the 2026 Form 6000 instructions. Articles: Read from the Alaska Legislature's site (Alaska Statutes 2025) in Chrome, because akleg.gov refuses scripted downloads. (3) is worded as conditional but applies to every corporation formed today. (5) covers a single class of shares. A corporation with more than one class, or with series, must instead set out the class and series details in (6)(A)-(C), not quoted here. The Division of Corporations' June 2026 compilation has an extra (6)(D) and different punctuation in (6). That may reflect a 2026 amendment not yet in the 2025 online edition, but it does not affect (1)-(5). Alaska does not require incorporator names in the articles; incorporators sign them under AS 10.06.205.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more natural persons at least 18 years of age may act as incorporators of a corporation by signing and delivering to the commissioner an original and an exact copy of the articles of incorporation for the corporation.

items.text: The articles of incorporation must set out (1) the name of the corporation;

(2) the purpose or purposes for which the corporation is organized, which may be stated to be, or to include, the transaction of any or all lawful business for which corporations may be incorporated under this chapter;
(3) if incorporation is after March 24, 1982, the address of its initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent;
(4) the name and address of each alien affiliate or a statement that there are no alien affiliates;
(5) if the corporation is authorized to issue only one class of shares, the total number of shares that the corporation is authorized to issue;

jurisdictions.name: Arizona
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; officers as set in the bylaws (one person may hold several); no residency or capital requirement; a statutory agent in Arizona; an annual report each year ($45).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain a word such as "corporation", "company", "incorporated" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Flat 4.9% corporate income tax on Arizona taxable income for tax year 2026 (the rate since 2017), with a $50 minimum tax.
jurisdictions.notes: A.R.S. 10-803 sets the number of directors, 10-201 the incorporators, 10-840 the officers, 10-501 the statutory agent and 10-1622 the annual report. Articles must be filed together with a certificate of disclosure (10-201). The $45 annual report fee ($80 expedited) is from the Arizona Corporation Commission's corporations fee schedule, Rev. 2026: https://www.azcc.gov/docs/default-source/corps-files/fee-schedules/fee-schedule-corporations6def4cc74b1a47129d16c2b1c3851bda.pdf. A secondary source says the ACC moved all filings to a new portal on 2 January 2026. Articles: Read from azleg.gov; 10-201 is at https://www.azleg.gov/ars/10/00201.htm. Two items are left out because they apply only in some cases. (A)(6) asks for the street address of the known place of business only 'if different from that of its statutory agent'. (A)(8) covers 'any provision elected by the incorporators' that must appear in the articles to take effect. A separate certificate of disclosure must be filed with the articles; its contents are in 10-202(D).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation and a certificate of disclosure to the commission for filing.

items.text: A. The articles of incorporation shall set forth: 1. A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 10-401.
2. The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue.
3. A brief statement of the character of business that the corporation initially intends to actually conduct in this state.
4. The name and address of each person who is to serve as a director until a successor is elected and qualifies.
5. The name, street address and signature of the corporation's statutory agent.
7. The name and address of each incorporator.
9. The signatures of all incorporators.

jurisdictions.name: California
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: Three or more directors (one or two with one or two shareholders); one or more incorporators; a president or chair, secretary and CFO (one person may hold all); no residency or capital rule; registered agent; annual Statement of Information ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must be distinguishable from other corporations on record and not misleading; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: 8.84% flat corporation franchise (income) tax for tax year 2026, with an $800 minimum franchise tax each year; a newly incorporated corporation is exempt from the minimum tax in its first taxable year.
jurisdictions.notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocked automated access, so I read the text of Corporations Code 212, 312, 200, 201 and 1502 from the california.public.law mirror. Before shares are issued, one or two directors are also allowed. The 8.84% rate is from https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/tax-rates.html (last updated 09/24/2025). The $25 Statement of Information fee is from the SI-550 form instructions as reported in search results; I did not see it on a live SOS fee page. Articles: Read from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov in Chrome, because the site refuses scripted downloads. § 200 is at https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=200. Trimmed with '…': (a) after the name (the rest concerns close corporations), and (b)(1)(A) before the professional-corporation alternative (B). Left out as conditional: (b)(2)-(4) for banks, insurers and professional corporations; (e), a mailing address only 'if different'; and (g), the class and series details when there is more than one class. Under § 200(b), the articles are signed by the initial directors if named, otherwise by the incorporators. The articles need not list incorporator names.

who_may_incorporate.text: (a) One or more natural persons, partnerships, associations or corporations, domestic or foreign, may form a corporation under this division by executing and filing articles of incorporation.

items.text: The articles of incorporation shall set forth: (a) The name of the corporation; …

(b) (1) The applicable one of the following statements: (A) The purpose of the corporation is to engage in any lawful act or activity for which a corporation may be organized under the General Corporation Law of California other than the banking business, the trust company business or the practice of a profession permitted to be incorporated by the California Corporations Code; …
(c) The name and street address in this state of the corporation’s initial agent for service of process in accordance with subdivision (b) of Section 1502.
(d) The initial street address of its principal office.
(f) If the corporation is authorized to issue only one class of shares, the total number of shares which the corporation is authorized to issue.

jurisdictions.name: Colorado
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators (18+); officers as set in the bylaws or by the board; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Colorado; an annual periodic report ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company", "limited" or an abbreviation and be distinguishable on the Secretary of State's records; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Flat 4.4% corporate income tax for tax year 2026, which can be cut temporarily (to as low as 4.25%) in years when a TABOR revenue surplus triggers the statutory reduction.
jurisdictions.notes: I read C.R.S. 7-108-103 (directors), 7-102-101 (incorporators), 7-108-301 (officers), 7-90-701 (agent) and 7-90-601 (names) from the colorado.public.law mirror of the official title 7 PDF. The $25 periodic report fee took effect 1 July 2024 (SOS press release). That release tied the increase to costs through FY2025-26, so check whether the fee changed after that. The Department of Revenue's rate table shows 4.4% only through tax year 2025. 4.4% for 2026 is the statutory rate absent a TABOR-triggered cut, and the DOR has not yet published a 2026 figure. HB 26-1289 (2026) makes worldwide combined reporting the default from tax year 2027; I did not confirm that the governor signed it. Articles: Not read from the LexisNexis public site. Its search found 7-102-102, but opening the section led to a CAPTCHA ('Captcha Validation' page), which I did not attempt, and I closed the tab. The excerpts come instead from the Office of Legislative Legal Services' 'Colorado Revised Statutes 2024' title 7 PDF on leg.colorado.gov, which is marked 'Uncertified Printout'; no 2025 PDF was found at the matching address. The Lexis search snippet showed the same wording for (1)(a)-(e). I did not confirm whether 2025 or 2026 legislation amended 7-102-101 or 7-102-102. (1)(b) cross-refers to 7-106-101, which sets the required share terms (classes and number of shares).

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state, for filing pursuant to part 3 of article 90 of this title. An incorporator who is an individual shall be of the age of eighteen years or older.

items.text: (1) The articles of incorporation shall state: (a) The domestic entity name for the corporation, which domestic entity name shall comply with part 6 of article 90 of this title;
(b) The information regarding shares required by section 7-106-101;
(c) The registered agent name and registered agent address of the corporation's initial registered agent;
(d) The principal office address of the corporation's initial principal office;
(e) The true name and mailing address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Hawaii
jurisdictions.office: Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, Business Registration Division
jurisdictions.security_registry: Bureau of Conveyances (UCC filings)
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; officers as set in the bylaws (one person may hold several); no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Hawaii; an annual report each year ($15).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated" or "limited" (or Corp., Inc., Ltd.) and must not be substantially identical to an existing name; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Graduated corporate income tax for tax year 2026: 4.4% on the first $25,000 of taxable income, 5.4% from $25,000 to $100,000, and 6.4% above $100,000.
jurisdictions.notes: HRS 414-193 sets the number of directors, 414-31 the incorporators, 414-231 the officers (no specific titles required) and 414-472 the annual report. The registered agent rule is in the DCCA information sheet DC-INFO. The $15 annual report fee is the 'filing fee' column on https://cca.hawaii.gov/breg/registration/dpc/fees/. Other sources cite $12.50 for online filing, so the online amount may differ. The tax brackets come from the Department of Taxation's outline current as of 1 July 2025 (HRS 235-71). I found no 2026 outline and no change to the corporate rates. Articles: Read from the Hawaii Legislature's current HRS pages on data.capitol.hawaii.gov; § 414-31 is at https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/hrscurrent/Vol08_Ch0401-0429/HRS0414/HRS_0414-0031.htm. Section 425R-4(a), cited in (a)(3), is the registered-agent information (Hawaii's Model Registered Agents Act); I did not quote it.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the department director for filing.

items.text: (a) The articles of incorporation shall set forth: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of section 414-51;
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(3) The mailing address of the corporation's initial principal office and the information required by section 425R-4(a); and
(4) The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Idaho
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of State, Business and Trademarks
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; officers as set in the bylaws; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Idaho; an annual report each year (no fee).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must be distinguishable on the Secretary of State's records (words like "Inc." alone do not distinguish); numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Flat 5.3% corporate income tax for tax year 2026 (cut from 5.695% starting in 2025), plus a $10 permanent building fund tax per corporation; filing the annual report is free.
jurisdictions.notes: Idaho Code 30-29-803 sets the number of directors, 30-29-201 the incorporators and 30-29-840 the officers. The annual report is required by 30-21-213 and carries no fee under 30-21-214, though a $20 surcharge applies to manually entered paper forms. The Tax Commission's rate history lists 5.3% for 2025 and has no 2026 entry. H.B. 40 (2025) set the rate at 5.3%. A 2026 bill, H0589, would have changed rates from 2028 but stayed in committee, and I found no enacted 2026 rate change. Articles: Read from legislature.idaho.gov; § 30-29-201 is at https://legislature.idaho.gov/statutesrules/idstat/Title30/T30CH29/SECT30-29-201/. Section 30-21-404(a), cited in (a)(3), covers the registered agent information; I did not quote it.

who_may_incorporate.text: One (1) or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: (a) The articles of incorporation must set forth: (1) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of sections 30-21-301 and 30-21-302(a), Idaho Code;
(2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(3) The information required by section 30-21-404(a), Idaho Code; and
(4) The name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Montana
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Lien Information
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; officers as set in the bylaws (one person may hold several); no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Montana; an annual report by 15 April ($20).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Flat 6.75% corporate income tax for tax year 2026 (7% for water's-edge filers) with a $50 minimum; a corporation whose only Montana activity is sales of $100,000 or less may pay 0.5% of sales instead.
jurisdictions.notes: MCA 35-14-803 (2025) sets the number of directors, 35-14-201 the incorporators and 35-14-840 the officers. The Secretary of State waived the $20 annual report fee for on-time filers in 2024, 2025 and 2026, and reportedly also for 2027; a late report costs $35. I confirmed the waiver and fees through sosmt.gov search results only, because sosmt.gov blocked direct page access. Articles: Read from the Montana Legislature's MCA 2025 pages; 35-14-201 is at https://leg.mt.gov/bills/mca/title_0350/chapter_0140/part_0020/section_0010/0350-0140-0020-0010.html.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: (1) The articles of incorporation must set forth: (a) a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of 35-14-401;
(b) the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(c) the street and mailing addresses of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office; and
(d) the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Nevada
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (natural persons 18+) and incorporators; a president, secretary and treasurer (one person may hold all); no residency or capital rule; a Nevada registered agent; annual list (from $150) plus $500 business licence.
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must be distinguishable from names on file with the Secretary of State; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: No corporate income tax. Instead, a Commerce Tax on Nevada gross revenue above $4 million a year (industry rates about 0.051%-0.331%; fiscal year ending June 2026) and a $500 annual business licence fee.
jurisdictions.notes: leg.state.nv.us blocked automated access, so I read NRS 78.115, 78.130, 78.030, 78.039, 78.150 and 76.130 from the nevada.public.law mirror. The annual list fee starts at $150 and rises with the value of authorized shares. The $500 licence fee for corporations is in NRS 76.130(2). The Commerce Tax rate range comes from NRS 363C and a 2016 professional article plus legislative tables; I did not verify it against a current Department of Taxation rate table. A payroll-based Modified Business Tax also applies, and its rates are not covered here. Articles: NOT read from the official site. leg.state.nv.us blocked access both to scripts and in Chrome (a Cloudflare 'Sorry, you have been blocked' page). The excerpts come from the nevada.public.law copies, https://nevada.public.law/statutes/nrs_78.035 and https://nevada.public.law/statutes/nrs_78.030, which cite the official NRS page (accessed May 26, 2025). Changes from the 2025 session may therefore be missing. (1) is trimmed after the name; the rest is a rule on names that look like a natural person's. NRS 77.310, cited in (2), is the registered agent information.

who_may_incorporate.text: 1. One or more persons may establish a corporation for the transaction of any lawful business, or to promote or conduct any legitimate object or purpose, pursuant and subject to the requirements of this chapter, by signing and filing in the Office of the Secretary of State articles of incorporation.

items.text: The articles of incorporation must set forth: 1. The name of the corporation. …
2. The information required pursuant to NRS 77.310.

3. The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue and, if more than one class or series of stock is authorized, the classes, the series and the number of shares of each class or series which the corporation is authorized to issue, unless the articles authorize the board of directors to fix and determine in a resolution the classes, series and numbers of each class or series as provided in NRS 78.195 and 78.196.

4. The names and addresses, either residence or business, of the first board of directors or trustees, together with any desired provisions relative to the right to change the number of directors as provided in NRS 78.115.
5. The name and address, either residence or business, of each of the incorporators signing the articles of incorporation.

jurisdictions.name: New Mexico
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC Filings
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors; officers as set in the bylaws or by board resolution; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in New Mexico; a biennial corporate report ($25).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain the separate word "corporation", "company", "incorporated" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: Flat 5.9% corporate income tax on all income for tax years from 2025, including 2026 (the 4.8% lower bracket was repealed), plus a $50 annual franchise tax on every corporation.
jurisdictions.notes: The official NMSA text (nmonesource.com) and mirrors were blocked or rate-limited. I took the one-director minimum (53-11-36), the officer rule (53-11-48) and the name rule (53-11-7) from search-result excerpts of Justia copies. I could not confirm the number of incorporators, so the minimums sentence leaves it out. The biennial report, its $25 fee and the $200 late penalty are in the administrative code (NMAC 12.3.2), and a new corporation also files an initial report. The TRD page confirms the $50 franchise tax. The 5.9% flat rate comes from H.B. 252 (2024), effective 1 January 2025, as reported by Deloitte and shown on the 2025 Form CIT-1. Articles: Read in Chrome from NMOneSource, the New Mexico Compilation Commission's official NMSA site (Chapter 53, site last modified 11/17/2026). It cannot be downloaded by script. The page uses several spaces after each paragraph number; the excerpts use one, and the check ignored whitespace. '[secretary of state]' in 53-12-1 is bracketed compiler text, not part of the law. (A)(1) is trimmed before ', if different, the name under which it proposes to transact business in New Mexico'. Left out as conditional: (A)(2), duration 'if other than perpetual'; (A)(5)-(6), class and series terms; and (A)(7), any provision limiting preemptive rights.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons or a domestic or foreign corporation may act as incorporator of a corporation by signing and delivering an original and a copy, which may be a photocopy of the original after it was signed or a photocopy that is conformed to the original, to the commission [secretary of state] of articles of incorporation for the corporation.

items.text: A. The articles of incorporation shall set forth: (1) the name of the corporation …
(3) the purpose for which the corporation is organized, which may include the transaction of any lawful business for which corporations may be incorporated under the Business Corporation Act;
(4) the aggregate number of shares that the corporation has authority to issue and, if the shares are to be divided into classes, the number of shares of each class;
(8) the address of its initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at the address;
(9) the names and addresses of the persons who have consented to serve as directors until the first annual meeting of shareholders or until their successors are elected and qualify; and
(10) the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Oregon
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; a president and a secretary (one person may hold both); no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Oregon; an annual report each year ($100).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company" or "limited" (or an abbreviation); the statute expressly allows Arabic and Roman numerals in a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: 2026 excise tax: 6.6% on the first $1 million, 7.6% above, minimum from $150 by Oregon sales; plus Corporate Activity Tax of $250 + 0.57% of Oregon commercial activity over $1 million.
jurisdictions.notes: ORS 60.044 covers incorporators, 60.371 the officers, 60.111 the agent, 60.787 the annual report and 60.094 the name. ORS 317.061 sets the rates and 317.090 the minimum tax. The CAT terms come from https://www.oregon.gov/dor/programs/businesses/pages/corporate-activity-tax.aspx. The $100 annual report fee is from the Secretary of State's business registry fee schedule as quoted in search results (https://sos.oregon.gov/business/Documents/business-registry-forms/br-fee-schedule.pdf); I did not open the schedule itself. Articles: Read from the Oregon Legislature's ORS chapter 60 page, 2025 edition.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more individuals 18 years of age or older, a domestic or foreign corporation, a partnership or an association may act as incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the office for filing.

items.text: (1) Articles of incorporation must set forth: (a) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of ORS 60.094;
(b) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;

(c) The address, including street and number, and mailing address, if different, of the corporation’s initial registered office and the name of the corporation’s initial registered agent at the initial registered office;
(d) The name and address of each incorporator;
(e) A mailing address to which notices, as required by this chapter, may be mailed until the corporation designates an address in the corporation’s annual report;
(f) The initial physical street address, including the number and name of the street, and the mailing address, if different, of the corporation’s principal office; and

(g) The name and address of at least one individual who is a director or controlling shareholder of the corporation or an authorized representative with direct knowledge of the operations and business activities of the corporation.

jurisdictions.name: Utah
jurisdictions.office: Department of Commerce, Division of Corporations and Commercial Code
jurisdictions.security_registry: Division of Corporations and Commercial Code, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: Three or more directors, or no fewer than the shareholders while under three (one before shares issue); one or more incorporators; officers per bylaws; no residency or capital rule; registered agent; annual renewal ($18).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company" or an abbreviation; a name counts as distinguishable if it differs by a word, letter or numeral.
jurisdictions.tax: Flat 4.45% corporate franchise and income tax for tax years beginning in 2026 (down from 4.5% in 2025), with a $100 minimum tax.
jurisdictions.notes: Utah Code 16-10a-803 sets the number of directors, 16-10a-201 the incorporators and 16-10a-830 the officers (who must be natural persons). S.B. 40 (2026) moved the name rules into Title 16, Chapter 1a (16-1a-302 and -303), effective 1 October 2026. The $18 renewal fee (domestic corporation, including a $5 surcharge) is from the Division of Corporations' Fiscal Year 2026 fee schedule, effective 1 July 2025: https://corporations.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/currentfees.pdf. I did not check the FY2027 schedule. The 4.45% rate (S.B. 60) applies retroactively to taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2026. Articles: Read from le.utah.gov. The text is the version of 16-10a-202 effective 1 October 2026, as amended by Chapter 92 of the 2026 General Session, which is the current default version. § 16-10a-201 is at https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title16/Chapter10A/16-10a-S201.html (unchanged version). Under 16-10a-202(3), stating the purpose as any lawful act or activity is enough for (1)(a). Section 16-1a-404, cited in (1)(e), is in the new Chapter 1a (2026). It presumably holds the registered agent information, but I did not open it.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as incorporators of a corporation by delivering to the division for filing articles meeting the requirements of Section 16-10a-202. An incorporator who is a natural person shall be at least 18 years old.

items.text: (1) The articles of incorporation shall set forth: (a) the purpose or purposes for which the corporation is organized;
(b) a corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of Section 16-1a-302;
(c) the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(d) the information required by Section 16-10a-601 with respect to each class of shares the corporation is authorized to issue;
(e) the information required by Section 16-1a-404; and
(f) the name and address of each incorporator.

jurisdictions.name: Washington
jurisdictions.office: Secretary of State, Corporations and Charities
jurisdictions.security_registry: Department of Licensing, Uniform Commercial Code
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors (the articles or a shareholder agreement may dispense with a board) and one or more incorporators; officers as set in the bylaws; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent; an annual report ($70).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must contain "corporation", "incorporated", "company" or "limited" (or an abbreviation) and be distinguishable; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: No corporate income tax. Instead, the B&O tax on gross receipts (2026: retailing 0.471%, wholesaling and manufacturing 0.484%, services 1.5%-2.1% by size), plus a 0.5% surcharge on Washington taxable income above $250 million.
jurisdictions.notes: RCW 23B.02.010 covers incorporators and 23B.08.400 the officers. The $70 annual report fee ($25 late, $100 expedited) is from the Secretary of State's annual report instructions (rev. 6/2025): https://www.sos.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-06/6.2025%20-%20AR%20-%20Profit%20M%26M%20Corp%20Sole.pdf. The service rate depends on prior-year gross income: 1.5% under $1M, 1.75% from $1M to $5M, 2.1% at $5M or more. Per RSM, the 2.1% tier took effect 1 October 2025, the 0.5% surcharge runs 1 January 2026 to 2029, and retailing and wholesaling rise to 0.5% on 1 January 2027. The DOR table gives no effective dates. A small business B&O credit applies to low-income filers. Articles: Read from app.leg.wa.gov; RCW 23B.02.010 is at https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=23B.02.010.

who_may_incorporate.text: One or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: (1) The articles of incorporation must include: (a) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of Article 3 of chapter 23.95 RCW;
(b) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue in accordance with RCW 23B.06.010 and 23B.06.020;
(c) The name and address of the corporation's initial registered agent designated in accordance with Article 4 of chapter 23.95 RCW; and
(d) The name and address of each incorporator in accordance with RCW 23B.02.010.

jurisdictions.name: Wyoming
jurisdictions.security_registry: Secretary of State, UCC / EFS
jurisdictions.minimums: One or more directors and one or more incorporators; officers as set in the bylaws; no residency or capital requirement; a registered agent in Wyoming; an annual report with licence tax ($60 minimum).
jurisdictions.number_names: No: the filer chooses the name, which must be distinguishable on the Secretary of State's records and not deceptively similar to a registered mark; numbers may be part of a chosen name.
jurisdictions.tax: No corporate income tax. The only annual state charge is the annual report licence tax of $60 or $0.0002 per dollar of capital, property and assets in Wyoming, whichever is greater (2026).
jurisdictions.notes: W.S. 17-16-803 sets the number of directors, 17-16-201 the incorporators, 17-16-840 the officers, 17-16-501 the agent and 17-16-1630 the licence tax. W.S. 17-16-401 has no explicit requirement for a designator such as "Inc."; I did not check whether one appears elsewhere. Tax Foundation also lists Wyoming as having no gross receipts tax. Articles: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 17 PDF on wyoleg.gov (file last modified 8 May 2026). The PDF wraps lines; the excerpts join them with single spaces.

who_may_incorporate.text: One (1) or more persons may act as the incorporator or incorporators of a corporation by delivering articles of incorporation to the secretary of state for filing.

items.text: (a) The articles of incorporation shall set forth: (i) A corporate name for the corporation that satisfies the requirements of W.S. 17-16-401;
(ii) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue, which may be unlimited if so stated;
(iii) The street address of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office; and
(iv) The name and address of each incorporator.
